Tech Report: Can global leaders put their money where their mouth is on climate?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1332 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The slow international response to climate change has placed the world on a path to destruction, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told heads of state and government during opening statements at this year's COP31 climate conference.
  • "The ⁠brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us," he said, as world leaders gathered in the Turkish resort city of Antalya to set the tone for negotiations at the UN climate summit.
  • A UN reportlast month found ​the world will cross a temperature threshold countries agreed to pursue in order to prevent runaway global heating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The slow international response to climate change has placed the world on a path to destruction, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told heads of state and government during opening statements at this year's COP31 climate conference.

"The ⁠brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us," he said, as world leaders gathered in the Turkish resort city of Antalya to set the tone for negotiations at the UN climate summit.

A UN reportlast month found ​the world will cross a temperature threshold countries agreed to pursue in order to prevent runaway global heating. At the same time, states like Germany are slipping down the rankings for climate action, according to the annual Climate Change Performance Index published Wednesday by Fresh Climate Institute and Germanwatch.

Nonetheless, Guterres mentioned the world has "the power to make sure the overshoot is a temporary breach.".

Negotiators from close to 200 countries are meeting in Turkey at the end of a year characterized by extreme heat waves and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a flood, killing more than 1,400 people and leaving thousands more missing.

At this year's talks, national representatives are discussing climate solutions such as increasing the share of electricity in an effort to move away from fossil fuels.

On Thursday, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, one of the few heads of government from Europe's major economies attending the summit, said that the world's dependence on fossil fuels was at the heart of both the climate crisis and energy security challenges.

"The shift to clean energy is the only route to energy security," he stated, endorsing the conference's focus on electrification which he said would lower energy bills, create jobs and protect people from the volatility of fossil fuel markets.

Burnham promised a "upcoming era of British leadership over the next decade," announcing the UK would put climate resilience high on the agenda during its G20 presidency next year.

The US, the world's largest historical emitter of damaging greenhouse gases, is not attending the summit — for the second year in a row after US President Donald Trump withdrew the country from the Paris Agreement in 2025.

Other nations, including substantial polluters like Germany, France, Italy, Canada and Japan, also opted not to send their top leaders to the talks.

On Wednesday, Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who is hosting COP31 together with Australia, which is leading negotiations, called on developed nations to take greater responsibility on climate finance.

Recent findings suggest that financing disagreements center around who should pay for international climate action, whether funding should take the form of grants or loans and how to scale monetary support for developing nations. Many of these countries are among the most vulnerable to the climate crisis but have contributed very little to the emissions causing it.

It has been revealed that erdogan said while previous conferences had resulted in different ideas around financing, they have yet to be turned into action. "We set out to make this an implementation COP," he told leaders.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen addressed remarks that developed nations are not contributing enough to climate finance, saying that the transition away from fossil fuels is in "our common interest.".

"Europe is the world's largest provider of climate finance. Last year alone, we contributed more than €32 billion [about $35.5 billion] to support developing countries," she noted, adding that Europe will continue to support partners worldwide in tackling climate change.

A recent Carbon Brief analysis found that public funding pledged under the Paris Agreement to help developing countries tackle climate change fell by more than 70% in 2026.

In a recent development, most multi-year pledges from donor countries expired in 2025. Since then, the US has stepped back from international climate efforts, while several European countries have cut their aid budgets, reported Carbon Brief.

Hilda Heine, president of the Marshall Islands in the Pacific, which face an existential threat from rising sea levels, said the response to overshoot "must be overwhelming" and promptly reversed otherwise "the world we know is over.".

"Every fraction of a degree of warming brings more catastrophe," noted Heine, adding that more warming makes it more difficult to adapt to living on a hotter planet, brings greater loss and damage from worsening weather extremes and greater financial need.

She called on leaders to triple climate finance by 2035 and make it easier for Small Island Developing States to access the money.

Sources indicate that "We are told there is no money, but their spending on war grows; the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death. Replenish the climate funds," Heine said.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese spoke of a "solemn responsibility to this and to future generations ​to act," adding that this is the critical decade.

Australia, the world's third-largest fossil fuel exporter, has vowed to promote the views of the "Pacific family" — small Pacific nations in the region such as Tuvalu or Fiji, where pre-COP meetings were held in October.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Albanese said it was crucial that climate cooperation delivered practical results — "unlocking investment in clean energy technologies, accelerating electrification, speeding up action for our oceans, unlocking climate finance for those who need it ​most.".

As reasons to speed up electrification von der Leyen pointed to wildfires in Europe and floods in Nepal, as well as droughts stretching from Central America to Sudan, and to the disruption to energy supplies linked to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

"The world is witnessing the cost of continuing with the status quo for our climate and our energy security," she noted, adding that the European Union would double down on efforts to become climate neutral.

"Three-quarters ​of humanity live in countries that import fossil fuels, hostage to price shocks they did ​not create and cannot ‌control," UN Secretary-General Guterres said, adding that recent conflicts have made clear a shift to renewable energy would help improve energy security and the cost-of-living crisis.

In a recent development, von der Leyen also expressed support for COP31's 35-by-35 electrification pledge. The pledge aims to increase electricity's share of final global energy use to 35% by 2035, with von der Leyen saying Europe would be the first "electro-powered" continent.

Heine of the Marshall Islands said electrification must must be strictly tied to renewable energy generation rather than fossil fuels, warning that continued oil, coal and gas extraction was a threat to her country's survival.

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said his country wanted compensation for environmental damage caused by US and Israeli strikes, including oil leaks from attacks on tankers. The strikes began in February.

Iran, which is a major fossil fuel producer and has pushed back against strict language on phasing out oil and gas at previous COPs alongside other petrostates, has also struck tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

Pezeshkian linked the glitch to climate finance and remarked his country expected "responsibility in times of war, to document and assess the environmental damages caused by military aggressions and to develop compensation mechanisms.".

Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who hosted last year's COP in the Amazonian city of Belem, remarked the momentum for climate action had dropped off at the start of the year, partly due to the Iran war.

"We started talking more about weapons and tariffs than the survival ‌of future generations," he remarked.

In a recent development, he also warned that "climate agreements are the favorite targets of reactionary forces at COPs," and urged leaders to work together. Lula promised to protect the Amazon rainforest. "Brazil is back to defend the continuity of a healthy planet," he said.

This article was last updated on November 12 to reflect incoming statements from world leaders.

Tech Report: Life as a Wag in the transfer window

📅 08 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1950 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Owen was on the phone to the manager and his agent while I was in labour.
  • Owen Dale's loan deal wasn't to a local club, but to Portsmouth - a city more than 200 miles away.
  • And the pair had only just got the keys to a house they had bought.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Owen was on the phone to the manager and his agent while I was in labour. They waited for me to give birth and then he went out on loan pretty much as soon as I was out of hospital.".

Owen Dale's loan deal wasn't to a local club, but to Portsmouth - a city more than 200 miles away. His partner, Jessica Beaumont, had never even been there.

And the pair had only just got the keys to a house they had bought. They would end up staying in it for just one night.

"Since living together, we've moved five times in five years," says Jessica.

"You have to be prepared for anything in the transfer window. But it's also a really fortunate position to be in at a young age.".

This period - when clubs are permitted to buy, sell and loan players - takes place twice a year, in January and during the summer, for clubs in the Premier League, the English Football League (EFL) and the Women's Super League (WSL).

While a select few stay in one place throughout their career, for most players moving from club to club is just part of life in the modern game.

It has been revealed that jessica met Owen when he was at Crewe Alexandra. A move to Blackpool soon followed.

"I didn't get together with him because he was a footballer so I never considered the footballer life - that he might just have to move at the last minute," she claims. "We just met and we clicked.".

But it soon became apparent that dealing with almost constant uncertainty would be part of that life.

The move to Blackpool was a loan, with an option to buy, so for six months - during which Jessica was pregnant with their son Xavier - they did not know whether he would be staying there or heading back to Crewe.

Sources indicate that blackpool decided to sign Owen, but he was soon out on loan again. This isn't uncommon, with loan deals a way for clubs to help young prospects gain first-team experience and get regular playing time elsewhere.

"When the move to Portsmouth happened it really hit me - I had to rapidly realise that 'OK this is now my life'," claims Jessica.

Just before Owen's loan deal to Portsmouth the couple had bought their first house together in Congleton - a town close to Jessica's family in Stoke on Trent, and commutable to Blackpool.

"We spent one night in there - we hadn't even unpacked," she notes.

They decided a 10-hour round trip on Owen's day off in the week to see his newborn son was not an option.

"We thought 'if he's not playing well because he's tired, what's the point in doing this'?" claims Jessica, who adds that they ended up renting out the Congleton house and have been living in rented accommodation themselves ever since.

"I was finishing my law degree and had a job at the time - I had to say to them I wouldn't be coming back from maternity leave," she notes.

Post-natal complications also made it difficult for her to travel at the time.

It has been revealed that "I had Owen on the phone basically saying, 'I've done a couple of house viewings. I've chosen this one. This is where we're going to be living' and showing me on FaceTime," she recalls.

"In that moment I did feel really out of control.".

Uprooting her life at short notice and leaving her family behind was challenging and Jessica remembers spending a lot of time alone in Portsmouth when Owen was at away games.

But she remembers lots of positives from that time too, including when she became friends with another player's partner.

"I was so fortunate that she would often stay with me when Owen was away," she indicates.

"I say to her all the time that I'll appreciate that time forever because I was just so isolated.

"Our schedules were the same - when Owen went away her partner was also away - I didn't have to be fully alone and she got it.".

Owen made 28 appearances for Plymouth Argyle last season.

Owen, now 27, has played most of his career in League One, with two stints in the Championship when we was with Blackpool and Oxford United.

In a recent development, last season was spent on loan at Plymouth Argyle and he is right now a free agent - this means he is not tied to any club by a legal contract. Owen can now join a latest team without a transfer fee because no former employer owns his registration rights.

Many of his moves have been on deadline day and he claims he is "very aware of the sacrifices" his family make.

Sources indicate that "There's always the risk that a move might not work," he states. "So I might uproot my whole family for this next venture and it all goes south.

"Over the years I've learned that until there's a contract signed on the dotted line, you could end up anywhere.".

Owen went on loan to Portsmouth in 2022 just days after Jessica gave birth to Xavier.

Owen returned to Blackpool the following year and made 32 appearances for the Tangerines.

The family moved to Bicester in 2024, as Owen helped Oxford United win promotion to the Championship.

Owen joined Wigan Athletic on loan the following year making his debut in a 2â1 FA Cup fourth-round defeat by Fulham.

Last season the family lived in Devon after Owen went on loan again - this time to Plymouth Argyle.

For now, Jessica's career in law is on hold, she instead has a job in social media and works from home.

She also posts about her experiences on TikTok, regularly using #wag and #waglife.

"My career can be picked up at any time - whereas his career is right now and you've really got to take every opportunity," she notes.

"As much as people say it's a glamorous lifestyle you do make sacrifices so your partner can have their dream and get themselves as far as they can in football.

"At the end of the day, as much as I'm involved, it's his career. That means in order for me to support him properly I can't get emotionally involved.".

This includes not getting too emotionally attached to where they live.

"We usually rent newer houses that are a blank canvas so we can make them our own, although this last season the accommodation was provided furnished by Argyle," she says.

"We put a lot of Xavier's toys and garden stuff in storage and referred to our Plymouth accommodation as 'the holiday house'.

"It can be hard when he asks us to get things like his trampoline which we don't have with us.".

Owen's career is always the priority, Jessica says.

"When Owen was at Oxford he had one year left on his contract and I loved it there," she notes.

Industry observers note that "But the best thing was for him to go and get game time somewhere miles away. So we moved.".

While Premier League footballers can earn tens of thousands of pounds a week - sometimes hundreds of thousands - life in the lower leagues can be very different.

"When you think 'Wag' [players' wives and girlfriends] and you think 'footballer', both of those terms come with this stereotype that our lives are easy," Jessica claims.

"People also put League One players in the same bracket as Premier League players.

"In the Premier League they're often set up for life - we can't live in that way because we have to prepare for life after football.".

Adding to the uncertainty of where they will be playing is also the possibility or relegation or injury.

"When we were at Portsmouth, Blackpool was still his parent club and they got relegated," notes Jessica. "Owen wasn't even involved that season, but his wage was still affected.

Recent findings suggest that "You have to be prepared for everything. You just can't live outside of your means.

"But it's still a really fortunate position to be in.

"Luckily, Owen's been good with injuries. There are some players who they get injured in the last month of the season and they're out of contract.

"In football things can be really positive or really negative.".

The uncertainty also affects their children - four-year-old Xavier and two-month old Etta.

"Now that Xavier is growing up - he's fast approaching school age - another thing that will have to be added into the mix is his stability," claims Jessica.

Even normal things like organising his recent fourth birthday party aren't always straightforward.

"We couldn't strategy to have a party in Plymouth with balloons and cakes etc because we didn't know if we were going to be there," she says.

"Instead we planned a party near my family in Stoke-on-Trent - we needed to make something work regardless of what happens with Owen's job.

"As much as I worry about Xavier and Etta, I also think how amazing it's going to be for them when they're older to be able to tell their life story and say they've lived in all these different places.

"I think it's teaching them a good life lesson that they don't need to be tied to one place.".

She says they have made every move a positive experience.

"We've mentioned to Xavier that we might be moving soon and when we do we're going to get his bike back out of storage," says Jessica.

"That way he knows that moving is a possibility and hopefully he's not thinking about what he's going to lose but what he's going to gain.

"The fortunate thing for us is that Xavier loves football. He gets a lot of excitement as well from the upcoming strips and the new chants and all of that kind of thing.".

Xavier has enjoyed watching his dad play at each of his new clubs.

So, does Jessica have any tips for people in a similar situation?

"The main thing for me personally - and what I've learned first hand - is the importance of keeping your own identity outside of football," she says.

"If you get too wrapped up in it, it only puts more pressure on your partner.

"If you can get a hobby, a routine or even a work-from-home job, that can help - things that can move with you.".

Being sensible financially is also vital.

"I'd also say that if you have a season where you get promoted, try not to change your lifestyle and to bank the promotion money so that you have as much stability as you can," she adds.

It has been revealed that "In our house, I de-clutter maybe once a month," she notes. "This helps me because I don't have control over Owen's career. But what I do have control over is making sure that if and when anything does happen, the house is ready to be packed up and moved.

"When it's the transfer window I will blueprint in one-week blocks - that gives me that little bit of certainty in a situation where I have no control.".

She admits "it can be hard" but "on the flip side it's so exciting".

Industry observers note that "We've lived in places that we never would have lived in. And that's exciting for a relationship," she adds.

"You know, with some relationships you can get bored.

"In football, you don't get bored!".

The ownership of Premier League clubs has never been so important. Years ago, football fans probably couldn't care less who owned their club. But now, you must have an owner willing to dip into their deep pockets to fund transfers.

Industry observers note that the likes of Newcastle and Manchester City are now essentially being owned by states, while there's an increasing number of billionaires in charge of clubs. If you don't have a rich owner, it's going to be very difficult to be competitive in the greatest league in the world. But which teams at the moment competing in the Premier League have the richest owners?

Given the fact that football has dramatically changed, and that those who have the most money tend to have the most power, these are how every single Premier League club ranks based on the wealth of their owners.

Brentford fan Mark Benham established his wealth through gambling firms such as Matchbook and Smartodds. He took control of the Bees in 2012 and also owns Danish side FC Midtjylland. He's become a bit of a hero among the fanbase with a statistical model helping Brentford establish themselves as a regular Premier League club, as well as helping build a brand-fresh stadium.

Sources indicate that brentford, along with Brighton, are two of the best-run clubs in Europe, never mind just in England. Bringing in young players that can be moulded and grown into stars in the making, and then selling them on to bigger clubs for a huge profit is the way the Bees have operated successfully to become a staple in the Premier League.

Sources indicate that in 2022, Acun Ilicali firm ACUNMEDYA purchased Hull City. Those in England weren't too familiar with the man, but he's a significant deal in his native Turkey. A broadcaster, entrepreneur, international TV producer, businessman and more, the 57-year-old has no shortage of ambition, and this is reflected in his sporting projects.

He's also had connections to Dutch football team Fortuna Sittard, Irish club Shelbourne, and was briefly on the board of directors at Fenerbahce. His sole focus, however, is now with Hull City, and that bodes well for the newly-promoted club.

Beyond Doug King at Coventry City, there haven't been many better owners in the EFL in recent times. The British businessman became the club’s sole owner in 2023 and has since restructured the club’s financial and operational framework in impressive fashion.

On the pitch, it was a bold call for King to get rid of the long-serving Mark Robins, who was sacked after a fine seven and a half years in charge, and eyebrows were raised when Frank Lampard replaced him. But it turned out to be a stroke of genius, as Coventry clinched promotion to the Premier League after 25 years away. Their net worth could be on the rise in coming years if the Sky Blues manager to cement their position back in the big time.

Industry observers note that tony Bloom made his billions through gambling, specifically poker. He bought his boyhood club, Brighton, in 2009 and has overseen their incredible rise with a clear philosophy and incredible success in the transfer market thanks to a data-driven approach.

Recent findings suggest that the Seagulls operate by using clever scouting methods to unearth gems from all across the globe to develop before selling them to the highest bidder. The best example of this came when Moises Caicedo was brought in for a nominal fee and became one of the best-performing midfielders in English football. This earned the Ecuadorian defensive midfielder a move to Chelsea for £115 million, making him the most expensive signing in Premier League history.

According to recent reports, US billionaire Bill Foley assumed control at the Vitality Stadium in 2023. He's the chairman of Fidelity National Financial, Cannae Holdings and Black Knight Financial Services. He also owns NHL side, Vegas Golden Knights and a stake in French Ligue 1 club FC Lorient.

There was an expectation that the beginning of Foley's time in charge of the Cherries would be in the Championship, but the miracles worked by Gary O'Neil and co in the 2022/23 season ensured the club's top-flight status. There was an influx of signings as a result and the appointment of Andoni Iraola has worked wonders as Bournemouth have pushed towards European qualification - though they must now start a upcoming era with Marco Silva in charge this term.

According to recent reports, after several really disappointing years, which saw Sunderland suffer two relegations and languish in League One for a period, the Black Cats have returned to the promised land. In their first season back, they qualified for the Europa League against all odds.

Majority owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus is the youngest chairman in football, at just 28 years old, but he also has one of the lowest net worths in the Premier League. Whether they can keep punching above their weight remains to be seen, but it's been an incredible journey up until this point.

Sources indicate that evangelos Marinakis, who also owns Olympiacos, hasn't held back in terms of investing in the transfer market following Nottingham Forest's return to the Premier League. It worked as they managed to stay up during the 2022/23 and 2023/24 campaigns and then flourished in 2024/25, finishing in the top seven and securing European football.

Nottingham Forest have signed an incredible number of players, which is a blessing and a curse as those players helped keep the iconic club in the Premier League. Marinakis is also not shy in making some controversial statements and decisions, one of those being when he hired Mark Clattenburg to become the Premier League's first referee analyst, and the other was boldly sacking Nuno Espirito Santo after he led the team to European football, before appointing four different successors before fianlly settling on Oliver Glasner this summer.

Recent findings suggest that joe Lewis is ENIC Group's major shareholder (70.6%). ENIC have been at Spurs since 2001 and, while Daniel Levy, who acted as the club's CEO for 25 years from 2000 to 2025 and was seen at every match, Lewis lives in the tax exile of the Bahamas.

Lewis was accused of being in charge of an insider trading scheme in July 2023, something that has been denied by the man himself. It is yet to be seen if any charges are brought against him and what impact that would have on Tottenham as a result. In the meantime, the north Londoners have been splurging on some huge upcoming signings to avoid a third successive relegation dogfight, with Roberto De Zerbi being handed a war chest that has presented him 39 new signings worth £237 million combined.

Leeds United finished first in the Championship just two seasons and will now be hoping that second season syndrome doesn't kick in. They have plenty of money to avoid the drop. 49ers Enterprises, who also own NFL franchise the San Francisco 49ers, have an accumulative net worth of just over £6 billion.

The West Yorkshire side splashed the cash in the 2025/26 transfer window as they spent £100m on new arrivals, and they are nearing that sum again a year on.

The Friedkin Group, led by American billionaire Dan Friedkin, completed a majority acquisition of Everton in 2024 which ended years of choppy waters for them under the previous ownership of Farhad Moshiri.

According to recent reports, TFG also own Italian side Roma, but their biggest move with the Toffees has been to complete their move from Goodison Park to the Hill Dickinson Stadium in 2025. The sky is the limit, it would seem, though David Moyes will need more fresh faces in the squad if they are to push further up the table and compete for European football.

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of vital saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

It has been revealed that alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

According to recent reports, “I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager remarked. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

In a recent development, “I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

It has been revealed that “We have to change our mind rapidly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”.

In a recent development, villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

Industry observers note that it was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

Industry observers note that mcGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”.

Suzuki has also flourished under Emery and he kept Villa in the game with some superb saves.

Robinson put in another cross and Suzuki got a touch that was enough to make Garcia put his shot wide. Villa were living dangerously and the Japanese goalkeeper made another outstanding stop to keep out Iwobi’s header. But then it all went wrong for Suzuki when he fumbled Iwobi’s corner.

That allowed Fulham’s recent revival under manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, to continue – they now have seven points from their past three games.

“We spoke at half-time about what we had to do,” Arbeloa said. “If you want to win a game you have to fight and I think we have to believe in our way, we’ve shown we can beat anyone in the way that we play but we have to be aggressive.

“We created so many chances and at the end it’s one point in a difficult stadium. I’m so happy with the second half because of the way we played, this is the team that we want to be.”.

Bologna coach Raffaele Palladino reveals he will punish Torbjorn Heggem for ‘over the top’ comments made on international duty by dropping him against Udinese, while there are injury updates.

Serie A returns this weekend following the break for international duty, and the Rossoblu aim to build on their run of four consecutive victories by taking on troubled Udinese.

However, Heggem will not be part of the squad after his criticism of Palladino and the lack of playing time at Bologna, complaining to the media in Norway that he “cannot keep sitting on the bench” for the rest of this season.

“When an important player like him doesn’t get as much playing time, he wanted to express his unease,” said Palladino in a press conference today.

It has been revealed that “Perhaps some of his quotes were over-emphasised in the media, but he too went over the top. This is why he is not being called up for this game.

“He is part of our squad, and although he will not be called up this weekend, he will be with us for the following matches.”.

The break for international duty was damaging for other reasons to Bologna, because some of Palladino’s players picked up fresh injury problems.

They included Italy international Nicolò Cambiaghi, who was so impressive in the 3-1 victory over France, then withdrew from the side for their trip to Belgium.

According to recent reports, “Cambiaghi had this ankle issue. Juan Miranda got hurt against Parma and will be out for another few games, but we’ll see if we can get him ready to face Venezia.

“I tried Alhassane and a few other alternatives in his position, but I don’t want to give the players any guarantees on who will start.”.

Among those contenders for the wing-back role is Federico Bernardeschi, who already played there for Fiorentina, albeit some years ago.

Nikola Moro in midfield and Ukraine international striker Artem Dovbyk have also struggled for regular playing time under Palladino.

Industry observers note that “I don’t see first choice players, but I pick those who show me more in training. Dovbyk returned from international duty with a different spirit, he has made progress and I am pleased about that.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Although Celtic entered the international break on the back of victories over Besiktas and Kilmarnock, the upturn in results didn’t quite lead to an outbreak of unbridled joy along Kerrydale Street.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 20 November 2026.

Although Celtic entered the international break on the back of victories over Besiktas and Kilmarnock, the upturn in results didn’t quite lead to an outbreak of unbridled joy along Kerrydale Street.

Since the first act of this season, a narrow win over Dundee, Martin O’Neill’s side have occupied a place of uncertainty.

Those who have taken the occasional stellar display to be indicative of a corner being turned have been left feeling like fools.

Sources indicate that there remain too many shortcomings in the squad, too many question marks hovering above too many players to ever feel that it has left inconsistency behind. The fan base has good reason not to quite trust it.

How could it be otherwise when the clean sheet claimed against bottom side Killie was the first in seven matches?

Kasper Hogh, the club’s record signing at £11million, hasn’t scored in his last 16 outings in green and white.

Martin O'Neill admits it has taken longer than he'd have liked for the newly introduced recruits to settle.

O’Neill’s options on the flanks include one player in Jota, who’s getting back from a long-term injury, and another in Yang Hyun-jun, who was recently sidelined for six weeks.

There’s a veteran in James Forrest, Seb Tounekti, not exactly the bravest of souls, and Haissem Hassan, a £6m signing who evidently believes defensive work is optional.

It says much that Callum Osmand, a centre-forward now trying to cut it on the flank, has become a fans’ favourite after just 13 senior appearances.

The concerns of the manager now extend to the middle of the park where Mika Baur may be out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage.

With Benjamin Nygren also a doubt to face St Mirren, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and/or Joel van den Berg could be teamed up with skipper Callum McGregor.

We’re assuredly about to discover if this squad has more about it than the results and performances to this stage have suggested.

‘We can make significant improvements, there’s no question about it,’ stated the manager.

According to recent reports, ‘Top of the league, it is nice to be in that position. But other than a number of matches where I think we’ve played very, very well... maybe the Besiktas game, maybe the Hearts game, it’s been really hard work for us.

Recent findings suggest that ‘That’s maybe a combination of things. Young and slightly more experienced players coming into the football club, getting to know the club, getting to know the players.

‘That’s taken a bit of time. I didn’t expect it to work immediately overnight.

German midfielder Mika Baur is set to miss around 10 weeks with an ankle ligament injury.

‘But they’re at a club where settling in is something they’ve got to do pretty rapidly.’.

Starting with the visit of the Paisley men, Celtic have 10 games up to and including the trip to Ibrox on January 3.

That encompasses two assignments on the road in the Europa League — Torreense and Omonia Nicosia.

O’Neill’s men also visit Tynecastle, Dens Park, Pittodrie and Tannadice in the league.

As they prepare to put up the Christmas decorations on the Celtic Way, O’Neill could privately be forgiven for wishing the festive season away.

January 5 is the day on which the transfer window in Scotland opens and you can’t help but wonder what Celtic’s prospects for the season will look like at that point.

While Camilo Duran and Baur have contributed, the bulk of the business done in the summer again looks to have been sub-standard.

To stand a chance of retaining the title, O’Neill badly needs several big-hitters to come in without delay in the Fresh Year.

‘We’re absolutely looking at players now,’ he stressed. ‘I suppose every single club is doing that. And the quicker you can get somebody in, the better.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We’ve seen when people are fit, we will have numbers. We just need a bit of quality.’.

Camilo Duran has been one of very few summer arrivals to have made an impact at Celtic.

Until such time as he can call for the cavalry, O’Neill has no choice but to make do and mend.

On the chances of prioritising the league and playing a weakened side in Europe, the veteran is clear.

‘Domestic football is really important to the football club, of course,’ he mentioned. ‘But you’d still want to try and make some show in Europe. And we’ve found that difficult.

‘I genuinely thought against Besiktas we did really fine in the game, we didn’t over-press because they could play through you.

‘There are certain moments even in domestic football when teams can play through you. Kilmarnock caused us plenty of problems.

‘I just think we’ve got to improve in the domestic games. We’ve got to be more aggressive in the sense of taking games to people and being less passive in periods of games.’.

O’Neill clearly needs more — much more — from so many individuals if he’s to get through the shark-infested waters of the next six weeks unscathed.

Hassan didn’t even make the matchday squad for Kilmarnock, a move which was interpreted by many as being a boot up the backside by a boss who’s been underwhelmed by his work without the ball.

‘We left out a number of players,’ O’Neill stressed. ‘I wouldn’t read as much into that, because a few will come back.

‘My job is not to please everyone, otherwise we’d have 26 players playing at one time.

O'Neill has backed misfiring striker Kasper Hogh to end his barren streak in front of goal.

‘I did a thing with corporate fans the other night, we had a bit of fun with some questions.

‘Apparently something came out that he [Hassan] was the most unpopular player in the dressing room, which is not true.

‘I didn’t say this. I was joking about my own unpopularity, as a player, because all I did was moan.

Sources indicate that ‘I did say about unpopularity, there’s at least one more unpopular. The crowd wanted to know but I didn’t tell them! I left it hanging. But it was tongue-in-cheek, apart from the part about me being unpopular, which I was.’.

Recent findings suggest that the form of Hogh is no laughing matter. The Dane looked the part when he claimed a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on August 9, but that is beginning to feel like ancient history.

For his effort against the Ayrshiremen a fortnight ago to be ruled out for an earlier infringement by Baur was a low blow.

Industry observers note that ‘For him, that was a killer,’ O’Neill reflected. ‘He has got the goal, gone off and celebrated and you just think... oh no, is that a goal?

Industry observers note that ‘He has worked exceptionally hard for us. But strikers live by goals and at some stage or other, he needs a goal.

‘The best thing for me to do is bring Henrik Larsson over and show him how to hit the ball into the net.

‘Shaun Maloney was telling me that for a little period he played up front when Henrik was injured for about a month.

It has been revealed that ‘And Henrik in that time was giving him advice about how centre-halves were reading him. He told him about getting yourself room, losing the centre-half, don’t be fighting with him all the time.

‘He scored a bag full of goals, so there must be something in it.’.

Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you watch the Bundesliga, then you'll know Wael Mohya is a fast-footed, quick-thinking footballer.
  • "Of course, I was absolutely thrilled.
  • "And the fact that it's come to this now is, of course, just awesome and makes me very proud.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you watch the Bundesliga, then you'll know Wael Mohya is a fast-footed, quick-thinking footballer. But not even the 17-year-old (Mohya turns 18 on December 31) Borussia Mönchengladbach youngster would have expected to be called up to the Germany squad so soon.

"Of course, I was absolutely thrilled. It means a great, great deal to me. I think everyone dreams of being selected for the national team at some point," Mohya mentioned.

"And the fact that it's come to this now is, of course, just awesome and makes me very proud.".

In a recent development, mohya was at the gym when the call came in. He then shared the good news with his parents over dinner. "They started crying," the teenager said in a video posted on Gladbach's social media channels.

It has been revealed that the youngster, who was born in a small town east of Düsseldorf, smiles and laughs a lot in interviews. He is always friendly, and in a good mood. On the field, too, he exudes the lightheartedness and carefree spirit of a 17-year-old.

As a technically skilled and creative player, Mohya often seeks out one-on-one situations and puts his opponents under pressure with quick dribbles. In nine Bundesliga appearances this season, Mohya has scored twice and delivered one assist.

According to recent reports, "He's so cool and just plays really well. It's fun to watch him," Borussia coach Alexander Blessin said recently.

It has been revealed that "Wael brings a lot to the team with his laid-back attitude on the field. He's not afraid to take risks, no matter how much pressure there is," added Gladbach's sporting director Rouven Schröder at a talk show on Sport1.

Borussia Mönchengladbach has been Mohya's sporting home since he was seven years old. Last season, previous head coach Eugen Polanski promoted him to the first team, and in December 2025, Mohya made his Bundesliga debut. Against Wolfsburg, aged 16 years and 347 days old, he became the youngest Bundesliga player in the club's history.

Recent findings suggest that mohya also recently completed a voluntary social year at an elementary school in Mönchengladbach. This is a program in Germany for young people who volunteer in the social sector — at hospitals, schools, or nursing homes, for example — for about six to 18 months. They gain work experience, help others, and earn a little money.

Recent findings suggest that at the school's open all-day care program, Mohya helped serve meals, assisted children with their homework, and played with them. That's also where his nickname comes from. Because a girl hadn't understood his first name correctly or couldn't pronounce it, she called him "Waffel." Now, that name has stuck.

It has been revealed that even before being called up to the Germany team, clubs in the Bundesliga and across Europe's top leagues had taken notice of Mohya and were trying to sign him. His contract with Borussia Mönchengladbach runs through 2028.

It has been revealed that with Gladbach right now in a relegation battle, his future appears likely to be elsewhere. If the club wants to generate transfer revenue from its biggest talent, next summer would likely be the opportunity to sell him — unless he extends his contract with Borussia.

Sources indicate that the 17-year-old's career is managed by his parents. Whichever club can convince them that their son is in good hands and help him reach his full potential likely has the best chance of securing Mohya's signing.

Mohya himself states he doesn't even know how much he's right now earning at Gladbach.

"My parents take care of all that," he told Bild recently. "I get a monthly allowance, which is more than enough for me.".

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp recently revealed how much he had enjoyed his conversations with the youngster.

"The conversations I had with him were great," Klopp stated with a laugh. "I wasn't that confident at 17, but then again, I wasn't that good either.".

It has been revealed that since Mohya's parents are from Morocco, their son also holds Moroccan citizenship. As a result, he could have played for Morocco, but he has now decided against it. In fact, the Moroccan football association had been actively courting Mohya as early as last year and had already reached out to him in the run-up to the 2026 World Cup.

Now, like Frankfurt's Younes Ebnoutalib, Mohya will continue to play in the German jersey, unlike Schalke's Soufiane El-Faouzi, who chose Morocco, or Bayer Leverkusen's Ibrahim Maza, who likely would have been selected by Klopp as well if he hadn't already opted for Algeria.

For Mohya, who played for Germany's youth teams from the U16s through to the U21s, the door to Morocco remains open, even if he does play for Germany. According to FIFA regulations, players under the age of 21 can change national teams before their fourth international match (whether a competitive or friendly match), provided that none of those matches take place during a World Cup or a continental tournament such as the European Championship, Copa America, or Africa Cup of Nations.

According to recent reports, if Mohya plays in the upcoming UEFA Nations League games in Serbia or against the Netherlands, another record is on the horizon. Although there were two even younger players who made their debuts in the Germany jersey — Willy Baumgärtner in 1908 (at 17 years and 104 days) and Marius Hiller in 1910 (at 17 years and 241 days) — the era in which they debuted is hardly comparable. And so, while Wael Mohya would rank third overall on the list, he would become the youngest Germany player in the modern era. The youngest to date was Hamburg legend Uwe Seeler in 1954, aged 17 years and 345 days.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence.
  • Recent findings suggest that is the climate totally cooked?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that AI companies must engage with those who oppose the expansion of data centres.Credit: Michael M. Santiago/Getty.

According to recent reports, around the world, people are demanding a halt to the proliferation of data centres — racks of computers, housed in warehouses, that are powering the boom in artificial intelligence. Communities worry that existing infrastructure will not be able to handle the surge in demand for electricity and water, and that data centres’ energy demands will cause environmental and health problems, including increases in air pollution and greenhouse-gas emissions. The question of whether AI is going to stall climate action is explored in the first of a three-part Nature Podcast (Nature https://doi.org/rzqs; 2026).

Is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

Recent findings suggest that is the climate totally cooked? What the data say.

People have many concerns about the way AI is being developed, including how it might affect safety, security and jobs. Where energy is concerned, however, any added demand for computing power can, and must, be met in smart, sustainable ways, not by burning more fossil fuels. Achieving this will take some creative thinking, and researchers need to be closely involved. Many argue that there are alternatives to relying on energy-intensive data centres, such as AI models that can run on individual computers or institutional servers, thereby consuming much less power than those run using cloud services. Efforts to develop such options need to be better funded.

It has been revealed that future projections of data centres’ energy demands are hard to make, because they are based on assumptions that could change. If current global trends continue, electricity consumption by data centres will go on rising. Between 2017 and 2024, it grew by around 12% per year. Figures for 2024 from the International Energy Agency (IEA), based in Paris, show most of this demand coming from three regions: the United States (45%), China (25%) and Europe (15%).

Industry observers note that the Electric Power Research Institute, a non-profit organization in Palo Alto, California, has projected that the continued growth of US data centres could add up to 94 gigawatts of demand by 2030, equivalent to 17% of the country’s electricity consumption. Data centres currently consume more than 1.5% of the world’s electricity supply, and the IEA’s projections indicate that this figure will more than double in the next few years. By 2030, data centres could consume more electricity than Japan, the agency states.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

Why scientists should lead the shift away from AI mega data centres.

Recent findings suggest that there are serious concerns that this extra demand will be powered mainly by fossil fuels, when carbon emissions are already at a record high. Research published this week in Nature Sustainability estimates that some 400 data centres in the United States accounted for around 26 megatonnes of carbon dioxide emissions between May 2024 and April 2025, more than those produced by many countries (G. Guidi et al. Nature Sustain. https://doi.org/hcsptc; 2026). And according to a study published last week in Nature Climate Change, data centres’ energy demands could prolong the lifespan of coal-fired power stations (C. Li et al. Nature Clim. Change https://doi.org/rzqr; 2026).

But none of this is inevitable. Governments could mandate that upcoming energy demand be met with renewable sources. And regulators could look at alternative ways to manage existing electric supplies.

In a recent development, many nations’ electric grid systems are designed to accommodate surges in demand, whether to power extra cooling on hot summer days or extra heating during winter cold snaps. Much of the time, there is excess capacity. This excess could be used to reduce the amount of fresh energy needed to power data centres.

How much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

Industry observers note that how much energy will AI really consume? The good, the bad and the unknown.

One solution is to curtail data-centre operations during periods of peak electricity consumption, and ramp up at times of lower demand. An analysis released in 2025 by researchers at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina, found that the US electric grid could accommodate 98 gigawatts of extra demand in this way, without adding any latest generation capacity (see go.nature.com/4cdeknm). That 98 gigawatts would be enough to cover most, if not all, of the expected expansion in US data centres over the next few years.

It has been revealed that there is potential for this to become a reality. In June, as part of a larger effort to modernize the grid, the US Federal Energy Regulatory Commission instructed grid operators to draw up a blueprint for how they will cope with extra demand from data centres. The technology industry is understandably paying close attention to how it might mitigate the problems of powering data centres. Earlier this month, OpenAI declared what it is calling a “grid protectors program”, a project to consult with US grid operators, regulators and policymakers to see how the manufacturer can work around peaks in power demand.

Meanwhile, Google is paying households and businesses in parts of the Eastern United States to reduce their electricity consumption during periods of high demand. Similar proposals are being considered in other countries.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

Why open-source generative AI models are an ethical way forward for science.

These are all tentative moves in the right direction, although arguably progress is not being made fast enough. Policymakers and data-centre operators must engage seriously with those who oppose the centres’ expansion. At a minimum, any newly introduced energy sources developed to power these centres must be renewable. Existing energy sources can also be better deployed, and researchers working to develop alternatives to energy-intensive data centres should be better supported. More peer-reviewed evidence is needed, especially for countries outside the United States.

In a recent development, there are smarter and more sustainable ways to power the growth of AI, but to achieve them, concerted and coordinated action will be needed. In this way, the harm posed to people and the planet can be minimized, and AI technologies can benefit everyone.

73 goals from dropping deep - we ask Kane to break down how he did it

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Harry Kane is one of the leading names in the race for this year's Ballon d'Or, having scored 73 goals last season for club and country.

As Harry Kane's career has progressed, the 33-year-old has taken an increasingly complete role, popping up to collect the ball as deep as his own box.

Many wonder why a talisman tasked with scoring doesn't spend more time closer to goal, but last season the England and Bayern Munich striker scored 73 goals - the highest tally of his career - while playing deeper than he ever has done.

When I mention this paradox, a grin spreads across his face.

"Until you really understand football and understand what we've been talking about, it's so easy to say 'stay high, you're going to score' but it doesn't work like that," Kane says.

I sat down to speak to Kane about the finer details of his game, shedding light on his unique role.

Industry observers note that watching Kane train, his professionalism is palpable. England's record goalscorer is one of the first out on the pitch. The younger players indulge in playful kick-ups as he watches, engaged in conversation with a member of staff.

From a distance, that makes it easy to confuse him with a coach but, given his role on the pitch, it is a fitting mistake.

Kane's style of play reflects who he is as a person, with those who know him saying he is well-rounded and humble on and off the pitch.

How dropping deep helps Kane score.

The season is in its infancy but Kane isn't basking in the success of the past 12 months. With only five days of pre-season training under his belt, the England captain completed 90 minutes of Bayern's 2-1 win over Borussia Dortmund to lift the German Super Cup.

In a recent development, as demanding as his roaming role is, he has taken the physical demands of it in his stride. Across the past six seasons, STATSports - a sports technology organization Kane has invested in - found his distance covered, high-speed running and accelerations were up 8%, 22% and 42% respectively.

And given how the tactical landscape has changed over that time, it is particularly impressive Kane has been able to not only keep up, but stay ahead.

Kane's role has evolved drastically over the past nine years, with the striker now heavily involved in all phases of the game -Â including as deep as his own box.

"Over the last five or six years, man-to-man pressure has become bigger," Kane notes.

"European football is physical and top teams are trying to win the ball back high, trusting their defenders and midfielders to defend man for man to win their battles.".

Given that change, the best teams have recruited physical athletes and brilliant dribblers who can beat their man when the game becomes a series of one-against-ones.

Kane, not known for his dribbling - and by his own admission "not the fastest", has thrived on his own terms.

Against Dortmund, there was a specific moment Kane dropped deep, looking to arrive in space unmarked. Recognising the danger, two players converged on the Englishman.

Industry observers note that kane's dribbling is cerebral. His speed of thought provides him solutions to problems others would attempt to solve with their feet alone.

After getting low and using his strength to shrug centre-back Waldemar Anton off him, Kane rose, slightly adjusting his body to the right. These micro-adjustments are a hallmark of his game and through them he is able to shift an entire team's momentum.

Fooled by this feint, Daniel Svensson and Jobe Bellingham found themselves wrong-footed as Kane snapped the ball back the other way, opening up the entire pitch from within Bayern's half.

Kane wins his individual battle with Waldemar Anton, shielding the ball and showcasing strength.

As he rises, he positions his body to the right, facing his own goal.

Industry observers note that through clever body positioning, Kane moves the opposition towards the right side of the pitch. This is his cue to cut the ball back into the open space.

This allows Kane to evade two defenders, now facing the opposition's goal.

Earlier this year, Bayern boss Vincent Kompany shed light on Kane's unique role, explaining it as being 50% coached and 50% Kane deciding what to do.

According to recent reports, "I think it's partly instinct, using my football brain and getting the feeling on the pitch," says Kane. "If, for example, I want to drop and see if the centre-back really wants to commit, he might commit into midfield, but is he going to commit if I drop all the way to my box?

"After the first five or 10 minutes you really get an understanding of how the opposition are going to play, which dictates how I play.".

In a recent development, in the second minute of Bayern Munich's game against Arsenal, Kane dropped deep into a position normally occupied by centre-backs. Arsenal centre-back William Saliba marked him all the way, vacating space higher up the pitch.

There is a shared understanding at Bayern of an approach that allows team-mates to make sense of rotations that, to the naked eye, appear random.

Kane, who is given more freedom than most, is at the centre of it.

In a recent development, "I feel like my position now is as one of two 10s, and you work together," he claims. "You can double up on one side to overload, which causes the opposition centre-backs a problem of who to mark.

"If they want to mark both, they've got to go man-to-man and then that leaves space for our wingers or full-backs to run into.

"It's posing all these questions to the opposition but, personally, I love having someone close to me who I can link with.".

Kane built his reputation playing as a lone number nine, so it is interesting to hear him identify instead as a number 10 -Â in a front two.

"When you're the number nine on your own you can get marked by two centre-backs and you struggle to get touches on the ball," he indicates. "You're relying on everyone else to find you with the ball.".

Showing Kane two clips from last season, I ask him to talk through what was going through his head.

In a recent development, "The thing with our formation is, as long as there's someone in each position, it doesn't really matter who it is. Lucho [Luis Diaz] in this clip is playing as one of those 10s.

"I've come off to try and create a bit of space and Lucho's gone through the centre.".

Industry observers note that distracted by Kane's dropping-deep movement, one of the opposition midfielders is pulled towards him. This creates space, allowing Joshua Kimmich to punch the ball through to Diaz.

Recent findings suggest that "I think it's Serge [Gnabry] making the run in behind which takes the defenders back, which allows me and Lucho that space in between. Lucho lays it off and whenever I'm in that position, around 20-25 yards out, I'm always looking if I can get my shot off.".

It is one of many examples of Kane initially dropping deep before scoring.

Industry observers note that "By playing deep when the play develops, I end up coming into a number 10 spot when everyone's dropped," he says. "I can get shots off from the edge of the box, which is a big strength of mine, or I'm running off the back of players where no-one's picking me up - because the midfielder finds it hard to [track].".

According to recent reports, the Frankfurt midfielder notices Kane dropping deep. Recognising this danger, he moves towards him.

With Frankfurt's central midfielder pulled towards Kane, Luis Diaz is able to receive a pass between the lines. He forms a central front two with Kane. The wingers ahead of them, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise, push the defensive line back.

Kane is found in space around the edge of the box and strikes the ball hard into the net.

The second clip is from Bayern's Champions League tie against Club Brugge.

Usually Kane is marked by an opposition centre-back, but the Belgian club give that responsibility to their holding midfielder -Â something he recognises and exploits.

Lennart Karl scores without Kane touching the ball, but the striker's involvement is undeniable.

It has been revealed that "These are the little runs, again, not everyone sees," Kane explains. "With Jamal Musiala and Lenny, they're so good at receiving the ball and dribbling so there'll be times where I will actually stay higher and let those guys get on the ball a bit deeper, and I'll try and make runs in behind.

"Without changing my game too much, I try and complement the players around me.

"I know Lenny is so good in those pockets and when he gets there, I'm more thinking of running in behind because, one, he can play me in and I can go through on goal, or two, he can dribble with the ball and do exactly what happened here.

"As soon as Lenny gets in that pocket I make the run and not always to get the ball, sometimes it is just to drag the defender away.

"Now he's one-against-one with a centre-back in the middle of the pitch and that's dangerous for any centre-back.".

Sources indicate that karl receives the ball in the middle of the pitch. As seen in yellow, Kane is being marked by Club Brugge's holding midfielder, rather than any of the central defenders.

Kane, recognising this, makes a diagonal run in behind, pulling the opposition holding midfielder away from the centre of the pitch.

Karl drives with the ball into the space created by Kane before putting the ball into the top corner.

Industry observers note that with the Ballon d'Or announcement on the horizon, Kane's name is in the conversation, primarily for the sheer volume of goals he has scored. What is easier to miss in that debate is the rest of his game.

Kane plays for the team in each phase of the game across the entirety of the pitch, while at the same time producing extraordinary individual numbers that match the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Erling Haaland.

He has described himself as playing in the role of a number 10, nine and six at times.

In a football world of specific and heavily drilled tactical roles, that is quite the achievement.

Williams-Barnett went so close to marking his Premier League debut with an assist but unfortunately Mohammed Kudus put the ball wide of the empty net from point-blank range after an audacious piece of skill from his teammate to tee him up.

Saturday's home encounter against Ipswich Town could represent the perfect opportunity for De Zerbi to give the talented star even more minutes under his belt.

There could even be an opening for him to start if De Zerbi sees fit as Mathys Tel, who Williams-Barnett replaced on the left flank against Crystal Palace, is set to face a spell on the sidelines through injury.

The Tractor Boys have fared well since returning to the Premier League at the first time of asking, after registering three wins from their first ten games.

However, Gary O'Neil's side do concede a lot of goals having shipped 20 so far, thus giving Williams-Barnett and his Tottenham teammates plenty of opportunities to attack them and cause some real complications.

More minutes will come the youngster's way over the coming months, with supporters desperate to get a real look at the academy ace from the off very soon as he can have a huge part to play in the club's future.

Luca Williams-Barnett's Statistics vs Crystal Palace.

Tottenham do have a decent set of fixtures coming up before they host Arsenal in the first North London Derby of the season on Sunday, December 6.

The trio of sides are currently in the bottom half of the table and they all look good opportunities to give Williams-Barnett some more playing time.

Ipswich appear the obvious choice for the reasons outlined above, with Sunderland a bit more of a test for the youngster due to the atmosphere generated at the Stadium of Light.

You would certainly back the Luton-born player to handle anything thrown at him, though, but De Zerbi will undoubtedly be cautious and ease him into the first team to begin with.

Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1038 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For members of the Indigenous Sasak community on the Indonesian island of Lombok, the conflict over their land is not over.
  • For them, a tourism and infrastructure project co-financed by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a source of frustration, as they believe it has led to the expropriation of their land and destruction of their livelihoods.
  • In late September, they officially filed a complaint with the bank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For members of the Indigenous Sasak community on the Indonesian island of Lombok, the conflict over their land is not over.

For them, a tourism and infrastructure project co-financed by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a source of frustration, as they believe it has led to the expropriation of their land and destruction of their livelihoods.

In late September, they officially filed a complaint with the bank. It remains unclear whether this complaint will lead to an independent investigation.

The AIIB, which finances major infrastructure projects across Asia, has a mechanism in place to deal with such complaints.

Individuals who suffer adverse effects from the bank-financed projects may, under certain conditions, file a complaint with the institution.

However, access to this process — known as the Project Complaints Mechanism (PPM) — remains controversial.

According to a report by The Diplomat, a magazine that covers political and economic developments in Asia, none of the 45 complaints listed on the AIIB's website had been deemed admissible as of mid-September.

The bank acknowledged that "no cases have passed the PPM's eligibility assessment," but it stressed that this is "only part of the story.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The AIIB emphasized that not every matter needs to be resolved through this mechanism.

The PPM is "only one part of AIIB's grievance redress ecosystem," the Beijing-based bank said in response to a query from DW.

Those affected should first attempt to resolve concerns directly with the project team at the local level, it said.

According to the bank, "twelve complaints were in fact resolved at the project level — as a direct result of AIIB's follow-up and intervention — and one was resolved through domestic courts.".

But critics see this as a major weakness.

"The mechanism must be easily accessible," mentioned Arntraud Hartmann, a development economist at the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS Europe) in Bologna, Italy.

According to recent reports, she argued that people affected by the projects, for instance, are required to document potential violations of environmental and social standards from the start. "How is the affected party supposed to know which standards might have been violated?" she questioned.

Sources indicate that the AIIB disputes this claim. "In terms of accessibility, we have made the submission form simpler and translated it into 12 languages," it mentioned, adding that complaints can be submitted online, by phone, or by email.

Urgewald, a German environmental NGO, cites another problem with AIIB-financed projects. For many of them, information on environmental impacts and resettlements is either missing or published late, it noted.

Sources indicate that for 2024, the NGO found that 11 of the 16 projects it examined lacked complete environmental and social impact assessments. In many cases, information on the potential number of displaced residents was also missing, it added.

"The information published on the bank's website is often insufficient and inconsistent. Particularly vital documents, such as environmental impact assessments or resettlement intends, vary widely or are missing entirely," remarked Nora Sausmikat, a China expert at Urgewald.

The lack of information makes it difficult for those affected to respond promptly and report violations early on, she underscored, adding that the situation is particularly difficult for people without formal land titles.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Christoph Steinert, a political scientist at the University of Konstanz, said the mere existence of such grievance redressal mechanisms "is not enough.".

Particularly vulnerable groups often know little about their rights, he remarked, adding that information should be available in local languages and targeted outreach directed at affected communities.

Criticism of the AIIB's procedures is not new. A 2023 report by international aid organizations, including Recourse, Accountability Counsel, and Inclusive Development International, revealed that the AIIB's grievance mechanism had failed to accept a single complaint since its 2019 inception.

The study highlighted that 101 of the 219 AIIB-financed projects, or 46% of the total projects at the time, were ineligible for review due to co-financing exemptions.

The AIIB typically provides funding without leading projects, a standard practice in development finance. When complaints arise, it directs complainants to the lead lender. As a result, nine of the 45 complaints fell outside its jurisdiction.

For Sausmikat, this is part of the problem. "The AIIB, however, decided against revising this requirement and established a mechanism that is very difficult to access," she mentioned.

As of January 1, 2026, following two years of external consultations, the AIIB reformed its complaints mechanism. Under certain conditions, complaints can now be filed even while legal proceedings are ongoing.

It has been revealed that but Sausmikat stressed that the changes are insufficient. Of the eight key recommendations made by an independent expert, only three were adopted, she underlined. "The revision did not remove the actual obstacles.".

The AIIB stated that the reforms are intended to make the mechanism "more accessible and responsive.".

The new rules have been in effect for only 10 months, and their implementation is being closely monitored, the bank said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Steinert noted fear of reprisals poses another fundamental challenge to such procedures.

Documented cases from Latin America, for instance, show that complainants have faced administrative or legal problems, and in some cases even violence.

According to recent reports, such risks could deter others from filing complaints, Steinert said. However, his research does not specifically address AIIB projects.

The bank said that it "does not tolerate retaliation against anyone who raises concerns.".

"Requestors may ask for confidentiality, and the revised PPM policy strengthens protection against reprisals," it added.

Sausmikat said Germany — as a co-founder and the fourth-largest shareholder of the AIIB — could also play a role, working with other member states to push for changes.

It has been revealed that hartmann also stressed that the bank's shareholders bear responsibility and urged the AIIB's Board of Directors to amend the rules governing the grievance mechanism. "We need a policy based on good-practice standards.".

This article was originally written in German.

According to GIVEMESPORT sources, the Red Devils hold an interest in Fulham duo Calvin Bassey and Antonee Robinson, with the former able to play in two positions the club are looking at strengthening, centre-back and left-back.

Chelsea defender Malo Gusto is also 'one to watch' in terms of United, with the Blues willing to sell, although they valued the Frenchman at £75m as recently as the summer.

Centre-forward is the other massive priority for club chiefs in the winter, with GMS revealing previously that there was interest in Dominic Calvert-Lewin at Leeds, although the England international is expected to sign a upcoming contract to stay at Elland Road.

It will be difficult for United to sign a new striker in the January transfer window, which is renowned as a seller's market rather than a buyer's one, but according to journalist Rahman Osman they may have found a top striker who's keen to join, Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen.

There is absolutely no doubt that Pochettino would sign Harry Kane tomorrow if he had the opportunity to, but that isn't going to happen after he won the Ballon d'Or and extended his contract with Bayern Munich.

Kane is a happy spot right now that has led him to football's greatest individual prize, and he has no need to return to the Premier League, yet at least.

Kane, one of the greatest strikers in Premier League history, has made no secret of how influential Pochettino has been in his playing career, and his two best seasons in terms of Premier League goals scored came under the Argentine's leadership.

A proper goalscoring centre-forward has become more of a rarity in recent years, in a world where Kane and Erling Haaland have excelled.

There is another experienced striker putting up ridiculous numbers too in Osimhen though, one of the best strikers in world football right now, who has been outstanding for Galatasaray ever since leaving Napoli for Turkey, scoring 69 goals in 85 appearances.

The Nigeria international was one of the main reasons Napoli ended their 33-year Scudetto drought when they won the Serie A title in 2023, and he has carried on that influence in Istanbul.

Osimhen, described as a 'Top 3 striker in the world' by Alvaro Morata, is a talisman who has so many different skill sets as a striker, and he would be ready to make an instant impact at Old Trafford.

The report claims that while the soon-to-be 28-year-old would be willing to listen to United proposals, he would want to earn a similar number to the £13m-per-year he is on at Galatasaray, who could demand between £80-100m to sell their star player.

Those are two big hurdles to overcome for a club that is looking to run more sensibly, but Osimhen has shown at his previous two clubs that he could be a game-changing signing.

💡 Key Takeaways
