What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1251 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.
  • The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.
  • "We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner confirmed after the talks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.

The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.

"We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner confirmed after the talks. US envoys Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Thursday, where they are due to meet President Vladimir Putin.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had earlier suggested an exchange of "1,000 for 1,000" prisoners, or "1,500 for 1,500." Russia mentioned a large-scale prisoner exchange with Ukraine could take place within the next two to three weeks.

Following the meetings, Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram that the parties had discussed security guarantees and that "the first step should be ending this war and ensuring Ukraine's security." He also stressed that Europe should be involved "at every stage of genuine diplomacy.".

Experts interviewed by DW agree that the main outcome of the talks is humanitarian.

"The agreement on a prisoner exchange is already a major step forward," indicates Artjom Bronzhukov of the Ukrainian think tank Polityka.

Pavlo Lakiychuk of the Ukrainian Center for Global Studies Strategy XXI also viewed it as a "very tangible result." He told DW that "getting our people back is already a major success. That is why it is worth continuing.".

A real breakthrough, he added, would be the release of civilian detainees from territories occupied since 2014, particularly people from Crimea, who have been held in Russian prisons for years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Davyd Arakhamia, head of the ruling Servant of the People parliamentary faction and Ukraine's representative at the talks in Abu Dhabi, gave a positive assessment of the trilateral talks with the US and Russia, expressing hope that an agreement could be reached by the end of the year.

"I think the Russians came with extremely strict instructions, and it was difficult to ease the tone of the discussion. But the way the US representatives structured the talks with a view to the postwar situation in both countries opened up a dialogue, in my opinion, and allowed us to work together more productively," Arakhamia stated at a joint press conference with US and Ukrainian representatives following the talks.

Iuliia Osmolovska of the Kyiv office of the international think tank GLOBSEC cautions against reading too much into the positive assessments of the talks from Washington and Kyiv.

"Diplomats taking part in negotiations will never say that everything went badly and that they have no expectations. Even when no results are achieved, they will still emphasize that the talks were constructive," she said. "For anyone familiar with diplomatic language, these are simply standard phrases.".

Osmolovska points to a joint assessment by 71 Ukrainian security and defense experts published by GLOBSEC in the summer. According to the assessment, the chances of a peace agreement or at least a ceasefire being reached this year or next stand at just 19%.

According to recent reports, she blames this on the fact that neither side is "ready" for genuine negotiations. Russia, in particular, has yet to accept that its objectives cannot be achieved by military means. "What we are seeing now is more of a farce, an attempt by all sides to put a brave face on things and create the impression that something is moving forward," Osmolovska said.

Artjom Bronzhukov sees the talks as a way for Moscow to buy time.

"The visits by the Russian delegation, particularly under the leadership of Vladimir Medinsky, are nothing more than an attempt to stall and sell empty promises to the US administration in the form of grand agreements, in order to continue receiving so-called gestures of goodwill from Washington, such as the lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel," the political scientist says.

Ahead of the talks, several Western media outlets reported on latest US proposals concerning disputed territories. The Economist, for example, reported on a proposal to redraw the administrative boundaries of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions. However, a member of the Ukrainian delegation stressed that there had "never been any discussion of concessions on territories occupied by Russia.".

Washington made no official comment on the reports.

In a recent development, kyrylo Budanov, a member of the negotiating delegation and head of the Ukrainian president's office, declined to say whether Russia had used the talks to demand that Ukrainian troops withdraw from the Donbas. Asked by journalists whether Moscow was still insisting that Ukraine pull out of the region, Budanov said the content of the negotiations would remain confidential until an agreement was reached.

"The issues discussed in the talks are matters for negotiation. The only thing that matters is the outcome. Once we achieve it, it will be made public," Budanov noted.

The head of the Russian delegation, Vladimir Medinsky, took a different tone, declaring that "every inch of our land will be returned to Russia one way or another." He was responding to reports in European media that Ukraine was rejecting territorial concessions.

In addition to the Crimean Peninsula, annexed in 2014, Russian President Vladimir Putin claims the four Ukrainian regions of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson in their entirety as Russian territory, even though Russia does not have full military control over them.

"Putin is not fighting over villages and ruined cowsheds in the Donbas. He is fighting for geopolitical influence and trying to exploit the collapse of the old world order," says Artjom Bronzhukov.

The expert from the Polityka think tank recalls that Ukraine was already asked in early 2026 to withdraw its troops from the part of the Donbas it controls and turn the area into a free economic zone. Such a zone "would very quickly become a Russian-controlled area," he warns.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pavlo Lakiychuk questions the idea of changing administrative boundaries.

"Why would Putin stop there?" asks the expert from the Strategy XXI center. In his view, US negotiators are seeking to extract unilateral concessions from Ukraine "step by step" without demanding anything in return from Russia.

Iuliia Osmolovska describes the proposal as "very original," but says it would pose risks for Ukraine's leadership. Even if the Ukrainian delegation agreed to it, which Osmolovska doubts, the decision would have to be explained to the public, which, she says, is not ready to accept it.

The GLOBSEC expert points out that, following the last harsh winter, marked by shortages of electricity and heating, only 5% of Ukrainians were willing to make concessions to Russia in exchange for an end to attacks on the energy sector.

Following the meeting between Jared Kushner, US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin in Moscow, Volodymyr Zelenskyy noted he wants to "coordinate positions with the Americans once again." No further trilateral meetings have been declared so far.

Recent findings suggest that iuliia Osmolovska believes the parties will sooner or later have to admit that the negotiations have reached a dead end. She expects each side to return to military action.

Pavlo Lakiychuk, by contrast, believes the talks should continue, if only to secure the return of prisoners. He is also convinced that Europeans "will always be there," because the matter is not just the Russian-Ukrainian war but the security of the entire continent.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 20:04 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 05:14 EST, 14 November 2026.

When Borussia Dortmund star Felix Nmecha transferred an imaginary crown from his head onto the pitch last weekend, he probably wasn't expecting to spark a firestorm.

Arriving at the German national team camp two days later, he was summoned for a grilling by sporting director Rudi Voller and manager Jurgen Klopp. His symbol of surrender before God, a goal celebration called ‘The King’s Return’, had blown up into an international news story.

Voller, alongside many of Dortmund’s fans, was concerned by Nmecha's ties to Ballers in God, a network of Christian players founded in 2015 by former Tottenham midfielder John Bostock.

While its core mission is to promote faith in Jesus, the evangelical group is believed to hold a conservative stance on concerns such as sexuality and gender – a perspective Nmecha has been in hot water for promoting before.

Nmecha insisted that his message was one of love, but as his celebration was dissected worldwide, the furore posed more questions than it answered. What role does the Christian faith play for footballers? What impact is the groundswell of belief having on dressing rooms? And what should teams do when ancient creeds clash with modern culture?

In a recent development, for months, Daily Mail Sport has been speaking with Christian players, chaplains, and academics. We have found that some footballers are still mocked in dressing rooms for their beliefs. We have also heard tales of elite stars praying with non-League journeymen, and of faith sustaining players through injury crises and rescuing them from dark places after their retirement.

Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha attracted controversy in Germany for his 'The King's Return' celebration against Elversberg last Saturday.

Manchester City winger Jeremy Doku is one of a growing number of practising Christians in the Premier League.

Sources indicate that for many players, their beliefs and careers are inextricable. Brentford forward Igor Thiago thinks it was part of God's plan for his father to die so that he would become a footballer and share his beliefs internationally.

'If my father were alive, I do not think I would have become a footballer, because I think he wanted me to be someone else,' Thiago tells Daily Mail Sport. 'It wasn’t until later that I understood there was a purpose for me to come here and be someone else. To be Thiago, who is a footballer, who can speak about God for so many people, in another language.'.

Industry observers note that thiago worked as a fruit-carrier, bricklayer, and rubbish collector from the age of 13 in the streets of Gama, Brazil, to provide for his family after his dad passed away. A career in the Premier League was unimaginable back then. Now he is the main man at Brentford and one of several players at the club professing a Christian faith.

Industry observers note that and they are not alone in their devotion. Across the top six divisions, 75 per cent of clubs have a Christian in the first team and almost half regularly host Bible studies or prayer meetings, according to a survey of 134 outfits by Christians in Sport.

Recent findings suggest that their director, Graham Daniels, remembers being told in the 1980s that he was one of just four openly practising Christians in the professional game. An impossible claim to verify, but yes, you read that right, just four. Now you have starting XIs containing more believers than that – and we hear some managers have even been attending church with their squad members. 'There’s a real movement of God within football,' one chaplain at a professional club tells us.

Industry observers note that perhaps God is dwelling in the treatment room, too. Bournemouth winger Ben Gannon-Doak has had three major injuries in his career – to his knee, then quad, then hamstring – and credits his growing faith for helping him recover from each blow.

Recent findings suggest that 'With the first, that was before I was strong in my faith – I didn't cope with that one well. I was 17 and felt lost without being on the pitch,' the 21-year-old tells Daily Mail Sport.

According to recent reports, 'The quad injury, I coped better because I started slowly practising my faith more. When my hamstring injury came, I was closer to God than I had ever been before and I coped with that very easily, it was much easier mentally than the other two. I was able to play in the World Cup after that.

Brentford forward Igor Thiago thinks it was part of God's blueprint for his father to die so that he would become a footballer and share his beliefs internationally.

Arsenal's 'Bible Brothers' are the most famous band of Christian players – around 10 of their stars including 'pastor' Jurrien Timber (left) pray together before matches.

It has been revealed that 'I believe all my injuries happened for a reason and I coped with them the way I did for a reason. I just need to trust God. It makes you stronger, prepares you for things, tests your character. It changes you. Faith has impacted my life in the best way possible.’.

Multiple footballers interviewed for this piece cited the Bible verse Philippians 4:13 – 'I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me' – as a key driver in their life. Gannon-Doak has it tattooed on his left arm.

Football has always had crossover with religion – Manchester City and Everton are among the many clubs to have started as church teams, for example – but the past few years have seen it assume more public prominence.

In a recent development, arsenal's 'Bible Brothers' are the most famous band of Christian players – around 10 of their stars including 'pastor' Jurrien Timber and Noni Madueke pray together in the hotel before matches, and regularly share Bible verses on social media. Organisations such as F3 and Ballers in God, who hold daily prayers and weekly Bible studies, have built Christian fellowship across the divisions.

'Premier League players are on the same call with guys who are semi-pro at step four,' Omar Beckles, a player for League Two Gillingham, tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Lads got together virtually during the pandemic and have been consistently since.' But why the explosion of Christian expression now?

‘An important factor has been the increasing number of players coming from Africa or Latin America, where Pentecostalism and other forms of evangelical Christianity are strong,’ Hugh McLeod, Emeritus Professor of Church History at the University of Birmingham, explains to us.

‘Chaplains interviewed for an academic study in 2011 claimed that elite footballers had “a disproportionate passion for the faith” compared with the average member of society, and they saw the players who had come in from other continents as having a significant influence on this.’.

An earlier generation of Christian players graduating into management positions, as well as a broader shift in Gen Z asking the cosmic questions in life, has opened up football to the tender matters of faith. Group Bible studies, or even stoppages for Muslim players to break their Ramadan fasts, were unheard of until recent years.

It has been revealed that 'Christians in a changing room can be frowned upon,' says Steven Sessegnon, the Fulham academy graduate who now plays for AFC Wimbledon. He was mocked for being baptised.

Marc Guehi was reprimanded by the FA after writing 'Jesus loves you' on Rainbow Laces armbands enforced by the Premier League in support of the LGBTQ+ community.

Daniels, who is now a director at Cambridge United, says Christian values have earned players respect in the dressing room – and thinks faith could alleviate the turmoil players face when the final whistle blows on their career.

According to recent reports, ‘There was tremendous bullying in the 1980s and 1990s, but the more people saw authentic Christianity, the more they realised that it didn’t harm the changing room, but made it better,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Their integrity shone through – players felt if they talked to Christians, they wouldn’t gossip, and they’d be caring, and they wouldn’t be judgmental.

In a recent development, ‘In football your identity is achieved. You're as good as your last game. It’s too much pressure for players. Tenerife won 5-2 at Badajoz in the Copa del Rey despite finishing the match with ten men. The victory keeps their cup run alive ahead of the second-round draw.

At the Estadio Nuevo Vivero on Wednesday 18 November, Álvaro Cervera’s side booked a place in the second round of the Copa del Rey. The tie had been postponed twice, first after the train accident in Toledo province and then after the death of Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel on 3 November, who was remembered with a minute’s silence.

Cervera started a line-up made up largely of reserves. It still produced a scoreline Tenerife had never recorded in 260 Copa del Rey matches, according to elDiario.es (Canarias Ahora). About 3,000 spectators watched, around 20 per cent of the stadium’s capacity.

Sources indicate that grant-Leon Ranos opened the scoring in the sixth minute from a Marc Mateu assist. Juanjo Sánchez added a second a minute later. Ranos struck again in the 38th minute, set up by Gerard Valentín.

Industry observers note that carlos Beitia pulled one back for Badajoz in the 49th minute. Roko Jureškin was then sent off in the 58th minute. Ten-man Tenerife still extended the lead through substitute Iván Chapela in the 69th minute, assisted by Martin Pečar.

Industry observers note that jorge Barba replied for the hosts in the 74th minute from a Manuel Hernández assist. Víctor Moreno completed the scoring deep into stoppage time, with Álvarez providing the pass.

Industry observers note that the Segunda Federación side went into the tie third in their group. They were also unbeaten in seven league matches in a row.

Tenerife have now come through their opening Copa del Rey tie in eight seasons in a row. The win followed a 2-0 victory over AD Ceuta FC. Before that came a run of draws against FC Andorra, Sabadell, Celta de Vigo II and Girona.

Sources indicate that this was the first meeting between the clubs in the cup. They had played each other 22 times in Segunda División. Tenerife won ten of those games, Badajoz eight, and four ended level. Tenerife’s previous visit to Badajoz, on 30 March 2003, ended in a 2-1 defeat under David Amaral.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the patterns of the international match calendar are well known at this point.
  • From the moment Mauricio Pochettino walked into a midtown Manhattan auditorium two years ago to make his opening remarks as the USMNT head coach, his presence has felt temporary to many.
  • According to recent reports, the cadence is unusual, since coaches rarely invite reasonable questions about seeking employment elsewhere.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the patterns of the international match calendar are well known at this point. Players pack their suitcases, board planes, spend a small stretch of days with their compatriots … and in the U.S. men's national team's case, answer questions about their coach landing a new job.

From the moment Mauricio Pochettino walked into a midtown Manhattan auditorium two years ago to make his opening remarks as the USMNT head coach, his presence has felt temporary to many. It was not just because job security is an increasingly unrealistic concept for soccer coaches, nor was it only down to the fact that Pochettino initially signed a deal that would expire 22 months later. The last two years have been full of reminders that the USMNT job is one of several that could be available to him – he has openly talked about wanting to return to the Premier League, did not deny that his representatives may have met with AC Milan in the weeks before the World Cup and regularly talks about his undying love for Tottenham Hotspur. The latest iteration of a years-long pattern came Tuesday, when reports out of England suggested Pochettino was a top contender for the Manchester United gig, which is not vacant yet but will be once the club finally parts ways with Michael Carrick.

According to recent reports, the cadence is unusual, since coaches rarely invite reasonable questions about seeking employment elsewhere. At this stage of Pochettino's tenure with the U.S. team, though, it would be difficult to characterize it as a surprise. It would be equally hard to argue that the pattern does not come with the territory, defender Antonee Robinson acknowledging as much hours after the news broke.

Industry observers note that call it What You Want: A weekly podcast where Jimmy Conrad, Charlie Davies and Tony Meola cover all things USMNT and the state of the beautiful game in the United States. Catch the show YouTube live every Tuesday and Friday at 10 a.m. ET.

"That news kind of got sprung on us, like the rest of the world, I'd say," he remarked. "Similar things happened in the past, happened at the World Cup where huge teams lose their manager and they start looking at possible candidates and for us to have a manager who's linked with those sorts of jobs means we're very lucky to work with a top-level manager but it never seems to leak into the work we do, whether it's the World Cup or whether it's going to be this camp.".

Pochettino's wantaway pattern may be annoying but it reflects the overarching sentiment of his tenure with the USMNT thus far. He is easily the highest-profile coach to take the job and U.S. Soccer is well aware of that. It is why they lined up donors to secure his signature two years ago to make him the federation's highest-paid coach ever, and why there is reportedly a $10 million buyout clause in the new deal he signed after the World Cup. For the first time in the program's modern history, they hired a coach with genuine international appeal. Even if Robinson should instead spend his time talking about the upcoming Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti, the fact that Pochettino would be courted by others was baked into his appeal.

Industry observers note that "Even when we first met a couple summers ago, there were lots of other people interested in having Mauricio and team join," U.S. Soccer CEO J.T. Batson mentioned in May as chatter around the Milan job took center stage in the early days of the USMNT's World Cup preparations. "He had standing offers from other places to come. He wanted to be here. He's a substantial believer in what we're doing at U.S. Soccer. He's a big believer in soccer in America and he's a big believer in this men's team and so, throughout this entire process, when you have top-class talent, whether it's salespeople, whether it's marketing people or whether it's coaches, other organizations want them and throughout this, Mauricio and team have been incredibly transparent. They've been great partners and are, of course, excited about the summer … There's been a longer list of outreach than what has even been reported and so they've been great about that.".

The key difference here is that he reportedly might be interested in United's offer, according to the Guardian, but the situation remains the same, despite the timing being strange, three months after agreeing a four-year deal. If Pochettino does not end up on United's touchline, his time with the USMNT was never destined to last forever, and U.S. Soccer admitted to it months ago.

In a recent development, "We actually, on a monthly basis, have a succession planning session for all of our coaches across all of our teams and so as a part of that, we have plans for renewals," Batson said on that May day. "We have plans for interims and we have plans for replacements because you never know what's going to happen. It's a global sport, lots going on and so that's a standard part of us growing up as U.S. Soccer.".

It has been revealed that many might spend the subsequent weeks after Pochettino's hypothetical departure questioning Batson's claim that the Argentine is actually a "substantial believer in soccer in America," though the argument is irrelevant as far as the USMNT goes. Pochettino's hire, along with that of U.S. women's national team head coach Emma Hayes a year earlier, was a large statement of intent from U.S. Soccer's leaders like Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, who are relatively newly introduced to their jobs. Pochettino's exit, therefore, would raise the question of how they continue that vision two years later, especially after outlining an ambitious path for the men's program in the coming years.

High-profile candidates like Pochettino are not exactly easy to come by, as the initial effort to hire him demonstrated. Ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola is easily the most notable name on the market but it is entirely unclear what his next coaching move might be, even if that should not discourage U.S. Soccer from reaching out if they have a vacancy. The options thin out from there if they are only to be measured on their flair, though, making it hard to envision a perfect follow-up act to Pochettino in the short term.

Industry observers note that there is a theory that U.S. Soccer may be resigned to picking from a locally sourced talent pool, something that is reinforced by a suggestion that Pochettino was a false steward of American soccer. His departure, if it comes in the short term, is not actually an indictment on U.S. Soccer's approach, nor should it encourage the federation to go for the safest pick next. Pochettino's tenure, at least up until this point, has been an example in reaping rewards for a bold strategy, one that should continue long after he is gone.

Pochettino's time with the USMNT has so far been characterized by mixed results, including some low lows that he bears just as much responsibility for as his players. It is not hard to see why he was a good fit for the job, though, and it is not because he makes headlines – his high-intensity, attack-minded style of play actually suited the player pool. The fact that he has coached in a UEFA Champions League final and won a Ligue 1 title with Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe and Neymar may help with player buy-in, but it would not have papered over the cracks if his version of the USMNT was not actually a decent marriage between his tactical preferences and the players' natural skillsets.

In a recent development, he continues to feel like a good fit in the post-World Cup months, especially as he oversees a generational shift in the player pool. Pochettino's tenure at Spurs, where he initially made a name for himself as a coach, was defined by his trust in young players but as it pertains to the USMNT's up-and-comers specifically, they already seem well-positioned to slot into his tactical set-up. The team's next great prospects are almost all exclusively attackers; Neil Pierre, the Philadelphia Union 19-year-old in the midst of a breakout season, is so far one of the few notable exceptions at center back.

A quote-unquote major name might not be a realistic option for the USMNT if Pochettino leaves now, though he may have theoretically made the gig more attractive to prospective coaches. More importantly, though, U.S. Soccer is now well-positioned to make a hire based on style and specifically an entertaining and effective style that captured the attention of an otherwise uninterested nation during the World Cup. Straying from that, no matter if Pochettino's successor is world renowned or otherwise, would not match the potential of the USMNT's rising stars, nor would it align with U.S. Soccer's own vision.

  • Industry observers note that palmer was shown two yellow cards in the second half of the Blues' defeat by rivals Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cole Palmer was sent off in the second half of Chelsea's 2-0 loss at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea's Cole Palmer will not miss the Blues' Premier League meeting with Manchester United on Saturday, despite being sent off in his side's last Premier League match.

Industry observers note that palmer was shown two yellow cards in the second half of the Blues' defeat by rivals Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday. That dismissal meant that Palmer was handed a one-match ban.

The England playmaker was shown his first caution for an off-the-ball incident involving Spurs' Mateus Fernandes. He was then shown a second yellow card for a foul on Conor Gallagher.

According to recent reports, in most cases, this would be served in that team's next Premier League match. However, Palmer will not miss Chelsea's meeting with United at Stamford Bridge.

Instead, Palmer will be banned for the Blues' EFL Cup fourth-round match away at Liverpool on Wednesday night.

This is because red card suspensions are carried out across domestic competitions rather than being specific to the competition they were received in.

Suspensions for an accumulation of yellow cards across a campaign are served in the competition in which they are received.

So while the Blues will miss Palmer for their trip to Anfield, he will be available to face United three days after the club's cup tie on Merseyside.

Real Madrid tie Tchouaméni and Güler to 2032 contracts within 24 hours

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (472 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Football-espana

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Real Madrid have extended the contracts of Aurélien Tchouaméni and Arda Güler until June 2032, a day apart.
  • Industry observers note that real Madrid have committed two midfield regulars to long-term deals in the space of 24 hours.
  • Both players are part of the core of Mourinho’s midfield.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Real Madrid have extended the contracts of Aurélien Tchouaméni and Arda Güler until June 2032, a day apart. With captain Fede Valverde also reportedly agreeing new terms, the club are securing its core midfield for years to come.

Industry observers note that real Madrid have committed two midfield regulars to long-term deals in the space of 24 hours. Güler’s announcement came first, and Aurélien Tchouaméni’s followed.

Both players are part of the core of Mourinho’s midfield. The renewals keep them at the club for six more seasons.

Tchouaméni arrived in 2022 and has made 205 appearances for the club. He has won eight trophies in that time. They include one Champions League, two Club World Cups and two UEFA Super Cups. He has also lifted one LaLiga, one Copa del Rey and one Spanish Super Cup.

In a recent development, his standing goes beyond the club. He has 50 France caps and won the 2021 Nations League. The newly introduced contract is worth around €9 million net per season, GOAL reported. The agreement came after interest from Manchester United.

Güler’s record covers a shorter spell. He was 18 when he joined. He has 38 caps for Turkey. In September he was named Breakthrough Player of the 2025-26 Champions League. His newly introduced salary is reportedly about €8m a year.

Recent findings suggest that the two profiles differ. Tchouaméni is an established international with a full set of club honours. Güler is a younger player whose contract now runs almost nine years from his arrival. Tying both to the same end date suggests a midfield the club intend to keep together.

Sources indicate that the club may not be finished. Captain Fede Valverde has agreed to extend his contract from 2029 to 2031, according to GOAL. The upcoming deal will make him one of the squad’s highest earners. An announcement is expected soon, as Madrid work on further renewals after Güler and Tchouaméni.

If Valverde’s extension is confirmed, none of the three midfielders would have a contract ending before 2031. That would remove contract questions over a key part of the squad for several seasons. The two completed renewals arrived during the build-up to a busy run of home matches.

Sources indicate that 🚨🤍 Aurelien Tchouameni has signed new long term deal at Real Madrid until June 2032. pic.twitter.com/13BtcLyubP.

— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) November 19, 2026.

In a recent development, tchouaméni has not been fully clear of fitness concerns this month. Earlier in November he left the France squad with a muscle problem. He was back in training with the Madrid squad on the day his renewal was revealed.

Real Madrid host Celta at the Santiago Bernabéu on Saturday 21 November at 21:00 in LaLiga matchday 13. PSV then visit for a Champions League game on Tuesday 24 November.

#25578. What needs to happen for Manchester United to get relegated from the Premier League?

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2585 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

What needs to happen for Manchester United to get relegated from the Premier League?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2585 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it couldn't happen, could it?
  • The table may not be telling us the whole story but it can no longer be dismissed like it can in August or September.
  • In a recent development, that is why Michael Carrick had to go.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it couldn't happen, could it? The answer to that is probably not but the fact that, after Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, Manchester United being relegated to the Championship is a prospect that can be discussed as anything other than rival fan fiction ought to terrify the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

A quarter of the season is gone. The table may not be telling us the whole story but it can no longer be dismissed like it can in August or September. You'll struggle to find many teams who can sincerely argue they've been mistreated by the fixture list and United are certainly not one of them. They are where they are, 18th, a point behind Coventry City and safety, and there is not much to explain that away.

In a recent development, that is why Michael Carrick had to go. On Wednesday morning, the 45-year-old was still taking training at the club's Carrington base but he is expected to be relieved of his duties once the United hierarchy have met in Monaco. There, the club's chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are expected to tell minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe that it is time to part ways with Carrick. Meanwhile, talks have already begun for USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino to take the helm, returning to the Premier League two and a half years after leaving Chelsea and mere months after signing a upcoming deal with US Soccer. It would appear that unfinished business in England -- and the Old Trafford vacancy to which he has been linked for so long -- has tempted the Argentine away on the eve of the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals.

According to recent reports, the path Pochettino is now on is one fraught with risk. And yet coaching for survival and nothing else would be the latest in a line of clumsy decisions from the Old Trafford hierarchy. Projection models such as Opta's would probably make the case that this team is dicing with danger but, with a 22% chance of relegation, will probably be fine. Bookmakers too are pretty skeptical that United's 2027-28 will encompass trips to Blackburn and Millwall with eight or so teams priced as more likely to go down than the Red Devils. That will be informed by an analytics profile that really does not suggest United are one of the three worst teams in the Premier League.

According to recent reports, through 10 games, a sample size where expected goals (xG) is more predictive than goals and scorelines when it comes to future results, United have an xG difference of -0.27. If there is an average team in the division, it's Carrick's. Naturally, that is not good enough for a team with their aspirations. Another 28 games putting up those underlying numbers and United will live to fight another day.

Sources indicate that suppose they don't. As anyone that saw Sunday's game can attest, events with a significantly less than 22% probability can happen all the time. A team's xG profile doesn't always capture everything. If it did, Villa would have notably fewer than their 13 points. Things could go worse for United. Let's have a look at how that might happen.

It has been revealed that carrick departs Old Trafford with his reputation among the fanbase still intact. He might also find that future employers look more forgivingly on his time at United. His tally of 47 points from 27 league games was bettered only by Manchester City and Arsenal, a goal difference of plus-10 putting United behind those two, Bournemouth and Brighton.

Equally, momentum had turned. With a full pre-season to establish his ideas (rather than hone Ruben Amorim's), Carrick seems to have crafted a team who are less effective in attack and more porous in defense. The 4-4-2/4-2-4 in which his team line up out of position has been easily manipulated by superior teams and structural issues are not offset by intensity off the ball. United rank 15th for pressures applied and 10th for passes per defensive action, both measures of pressing applied by a team. Meanwhile, the attack has both been creating fewer chances -- the comeback against Villa notwithstanding -- and being more wasteful with them. It is a bad cocktail.

Industry observers note that the risk would have been that United reaffirmed the commitment they made to Carrick after the three-goal defeats to Como and Bournemouth, one which always seemed to be conditioned on the imminent international break. Could anyone parachuted in at a moment's notice have done much better than four points against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa? The November international break has always functioned as a critical point for English clubs. Fail to pull the trigger now when there is time to get your feet under the desk and familiarize yourself with players -- who, for once, will have a few days back at the training ground after their commitments around the globe -- before the festive fixture list bears its teeth. In that context, sacking a relatively inexperienced coach like Carrick probably lessens the relegation risk somewhat.

In a recent development, so, in principle, does hiring Pochettino. Here is a coach with over 400 games at the helm of English clubs, whose first job in the country with Southampton has afforded him some experience of the tight margins needed to avoid the drop zone. It was his work at Tottenham that so enamored Sir Alex Ferguson. Over five and a half years he forged Spurs into contenders for (but not winners of) the biggest prizes in the sport. Aggressive, attacking football with a young side imbued with English talent: everything except the silverware screams Manchester United in their pomp.

Sources indicate that the price of that success was Pochettino's identity and Tottenham's intermingling. No bad thing when you are as successful as he was at first but it may have given the Argentine an expectation about his role in club football that he has brushed up against in subsequent jobs. At Chelsea he took umbrage at the hierarchy's insistence on affording him young signings rather than the veterans he wanted. The idea that set pieces should sit somewhat outside his jurisdiction and under "specialists" was not popular. At Tottenham, Pochettino had become accustomed to working cheek to jowl with executive chairman and part-owner Daniel Levy. Chelsea, like most Premier League clubs, have established numerous layers between the man in the dugout and the owners. He may not lose his rag in the manner of Antonio Conte but Pochettino is a deeply political operator. Any man who is not afraid to say what he sees could create a great deal of friction when he sees what has been going on at United these last few years.

When he left Stamford Bridge the sense was that Pochettino was yesterday's man in the rapidly evolving world of the Premier League, even though in retrospect it appears he left strong foundations for Enzo Maresca to build on. That view was clearly not one that senior figures at United entirely discounted. After all, at the time they were seriously considering sacking Erik ten Hag after finishing eighth in the Premier League. Pochettino was among the names they considered before doubling down on the soon-to-be-deposed Dutchman.

In a recent development, that was not the only time United could have got Pochettino. Indeed, when he left Paris Saint-Germain in the summer of 2022, he was interviewed before Ten Hag got the job. That was the most formal approach but there was also the restaurant summit with Ferguson at a Mayfair restaurant when Louis van Gaal was on the brink. And of course there was the chance to hire the 54-year-old in that window earlier this year when Carrick's interim spell was coming to an end and Pochettino had not yet recommitted to the USMNT.

Going for a coach they have consistently decided is not the best option for them will now cost them $10 million for his compensation plus the cost of his sizeable staff. The evidence of PSG, Chelsea and the USMNT is he can deliver to (realistic) expectations. In all likelihood things stabilize under Pochettino, the specter of relegation cast off. The scenario where he takes them down? It probably reflects yesterday's man taking a job at a club still enamored with an outdated vision of management. Pochettino is probably the most Ferguson-coded manager United have employed since the great man's anointed successor. His intense style of play will need willing participants and even if he finds them, it will also take time. That much was as apparent at the clubs where it clicked -- one win in his first seven league games with Southampton, three in nine at Spurs -- as it was elsewhere. Time is not a commodity a side in 18th place can really trade in.

According to recent reports, though Phil Neville was quite scathing in his assessment of Noussair Mazraoui, Ayden Heaven, Leny Yoro and Diogo Dalot on Sunday -- "that back four gets you relegated" -- in pure talent terms United should be absolutely fine. You can question how many players in the squad make up the core of the title-contending outfit they aspire to be but there has been plenty of decent business done buying decent players from decent Premier League teams. Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha, (in theory right now if not in practice) Youri Tielemans.

According to recent reports, getting another left back and another forward in January would solve a few issues created by more injury-addled players. Then again so would the players on the roster executing better. United rank fourth in the league for non-penalty xG but 11th for goals. Maybe that is because of their wayward finishing. Opta's shooting goals added metric, which assesses the likelihood of a goal being scored pre- and post-shot, ranks this team 17th in the league on -3.57. You wouldn't expect that to hold all season long, particularly when some of the worst offenders are Bruno Fernandes and Cunha. Of course, if it did, then yes, United would be in real trouble.

The same at the other end. Yoro met a free kick with a fine header at Old Trafford on Sunday, drawing a springy save from a goalkeeper who could not stop the ball being turned in on the rebound. The slight issue is the goalkeeper was Senne Lammens and that was the fourth error leading to a goal that United have made this season. Low-volume statistics like these can occasionally betray you but in this case it speaks to a truth clear for all to see; the United defense is too slap-dashy. Young and old, players at Old Trafford have learned that basic errors rarely lead to lasting consequences. If this clumsiness continues -- and it should not be treated as a given that it does -- then the crisis could deepen.

It's worth saying from the off that if you're rooting for chaos you'd want to see Manchester United's numbers trend down quite dramatically for there to be much in the analytics that says 18th or worse. The "best" relegated sides of recent years are probably Leicester City in 2022-23, sent down to the Championship on 34 points and -0.39 non-penalty xG difference (npxGD) per game, and West Ham three years later. They slipped through the trap door on 39 points and -0.26 npxGD, just a shade worse than Tottenham. Manchester United have sunk to levels below that in past seasons but not this.

Right now there is a long way to go to catch up with the worst teams in the league so far. Ipswich Town have accrued points and look to be a hard out but they are averaging -0.67 npxG difference per game. They are the worst of the newly promoted sides but both Hull City (-0.5) and Coventry City (-0.48) are delivering worrying analytics. The former have the advantage of those points they accrued early in the season and Hull deserve credit for how sparky and organized they are given the talent deficit Sergej Jakirovic is working with. Apply some of those principles with United's talent and competence is no longer the limit.

Recent findings suggest that it isn't just the promoted sides that look bad. Sunderland have a case of difficult second-season syndrome. The best that can be mentioned for Newcastle is that, like Hull, they've banked some fortuitous points. We can maybe ignore Aston Villa given how rarely their xG reflects the results Unai Emery gets.

Then there is Crystal Palace and, well, yikes. In the six seasons before this one only seven teams have had a worse npxGD per game than Palace's -0.86, which is a true marker of inadequacy. These levels Pierre Sage has plummeted the Conference League winners to aren't much better than Norwich City in 2021-22, Luton Town in 2023-24 or the carnival of ineptitude that was Leicester and Southampton two years ago. Palace are bad. So, so bad.

At least they are in results terms. The talent doesn't seem that bad even if the drip-drip of departures over the last year -- Oliver Glasner, Maxence Lacroix, Marc Guehi, Eberechi Eze -- has lowered their ceiling. With a Thomas Frank in charge you could see them move back on the right path rapidly. Maybe the northeast triumvirate swing upwards too. Suddenly then there might be a space opening up for a team that is both bad and unlucky. That is, of course, assuming that there are three spots opened up for relegated teams this season.

Of course Manchester City might yet have a spot in next season's Championship with their name on it. City were found to have breached 114 of the Premier League's rules by an independent commission, a verdict they are in the midst of appealing.

Industry observers note that separate to the process of establishing whether the commission erred in its duties is the matter of sanctioning City. That will be decided by the same three-person panel though it is not yet clear when the hearing will take place nor what the Premier League will expect. Given the abrasive language used by the league about one of its member clubs, it is hard to see them settling for a proposal that does not end with City out of the top flight at the end of the season.

It has been revealed that the Premier League wants this process wrapped up comprehensively but swiftly. Much of the football world expects City to get hit hard, hence why bookmakers have Enzo Maresca's side among the three most likely teams to be relegated. A sweeping points deduction at the Etihad Stadium would be greeted with delight around Old Trafford for many reasons. The fact that it might insulate United from their own mismanagement is certainly one of them.

There are, however, no guarantees that this process will reach its conclusion before the end of the season. City could endure, dragging out a process they have made plain they believe to be compromised at its most basic principles. Can they keep the wheels spinning for another seven-plus months? Or argue their way to the sort of punishment that does not send them off the edge of the Premier League map? It may be hard to do but it is the sort of unlikely event that, for the time being, might be required to send United to the Championship.

Industry News: Which Premier League players are set for yellow card suspensions?

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (526 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Harry Maguire and Alexis Mac Allister are among 13 players on the brink of a one-match ban.
  • The first one-match suspensions for yellow card offences in the 2026-27 Premier League season have now been served.
  • Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash became the first players to receive a ban for accumulating five yellow cards before gameweek 19.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Harry Maguire and Alexis Mac Allister are among 13 players on the brink of a one-match ban.

The first one-match suspensions for yellow card offences in the 2026-27 Premier League season have now been served.

Hull City's Matt Crooks and Aston Villa's Matty Cash became the first players to receive a ban for accumulating five yellow cards before gameweek 19.

Players receive a one-match suspension if they pick up five or more yellow cards prior to the conclusion of their team's 19th league match of the season.

There are now 13 players sitting on four bookings after 10 rounds of matches, meaning they must avoid another yellow card prior to the halfway point of the season to avoid a ban.

Bournemouth have the most players on the brink of a ban, with three players one yellow card away from suspension.

Recent findings suggest that after that date, the threshold increases to 10 yellow cards. Any player reaching that number before the end of their club's 32nd league match of the season will receive a two-match suspension.

From that point, there are further thresholds at 15 and 20 yellow cards.

Industry observers note that for players reaching 15 cautions, they incur a three-match suspension. Punishments for players reaching 20 yellow cards are determined by a regulatory commission.

Those cut-offs do not reset until the end of the Premier League season.

In the Championship, League One and League Two, there are similar thresholds.

However, with those three divisions having 46 rounds of league matches instead of 38, players have to avoid getting 10 yellow cards before the end of the 37th league match in order to not receive a two-match suspension.

In those divisions, the yellow cards are reset at the end of the league season and do not include matches in the play-offs.

The following players have served a one-match ban and will now receive a two-match ban if they reach ten bookings before game week 32:.

Matt Crooks - Hull City (five yellow cards).

Matty Cash - Aston Villa (five).

If any of the following players receive another Premier League yellow card before the season's halfway point, they will be banned for one match:.

Vitaly Janelt - Brentford (four).

Oli McBurnie - Hull City (four).

Harry Maguire - Manchester United (four).

Pascal Gross - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Ethan Ampadu - Leeds United (four).

Oliver Boscagli - Brighton & Hove Albion (four).

Adam Smith - Bournemouth (four).

Marcus Tavernier - Bournemouth (four).

Antonio Silve - Bournemouth (four).

Yeremy Pino - Crystal Palace (four).

Alexis Mac Allister - Liverpool (four).

James McAtee - Nottingham Forest (four).

The following players will miss their club's next set of fixtures:.

Max Dowman - Arsenal (red card suspension).

Jean-Philippe Mateta - Crystal Palace (red card suspension).

Igor Thiago - Brentford (red card suspension).

#25565. Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (823 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (823 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a company would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday.
  • "We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a company would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you. The proposed law would also make it easier to cancel a subscription online and require reminders before certain contracts renew automatically.

Recent findings suggest that the Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday. It wants to give consumers more control over how much time and money they spend online.

"We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.

Recent findings suggest that his organization pushed for stronger EU rules against manipulative online practices. He sees the proposal as a good starting point for tackling problems that frustrate consumers every day.

The proposal also includes a ban on manipulative marketing tactics, so-called "dark patterns." A concrete example: You are trying to reserve a hotel room and the website claims that only three are left, a potentially false claim to pressure you into buying.

According to recent reports, A concert ticket that gets more expensive while you're waiting in an online queue raises a different problem. The price could still go up in the process, but the seller would have to show the current price while you wait and tell you the maximum you could be asked to pay.

Online games that encourage users to spend their money to advance are also targeted. Children would no longer be able to pay to win or get to the next level of their online game.

Recent findings suggest that marketing and personalized ads would need to be clearly marked and restricted in the case of children. Consumers should get the option to switch off doomscrolling functions such as the autoplay of videos, showing one clip after the other. With these fresh rules, the EU wants to make apps and websites less addictive.

For Christoph Busch, an academic with a focus on consumer law and digital services based at Osnabrück University in Germany, the option to opt out doesn't go far enough. He argues that a version in which consumers actively have to choose to opt into those functions would be more effective.

Industry observers note that "But then there is always the question of proportionality," Busch stated. "And I think here the European legislators are trying to balance different interests.".

These competing interests are particularly visible in the gaming industry, where interest groups have warned that the proposed EU restrictions could hurt developers and leave players with fewer options to choose from.

Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation called the proposal "unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate," arguing that a ban on selling children features that help them win or advance is worded so broadly that it "could cover almost any purchase in a game.".

Industry observers note that for Busch, this argument doesn't hold. "If your business model is based on addictive design features, then maybe your business model has to be reviewed," he remarked.

Catalina Goanta, an associate professor of private law and technology at Utrecht University, emphasized in an interview with DW that "regulation can very easily slide into overregulation.".

Industry observers note that even though she believes that the DFA is a solid and reasonable compromise, she argues that prohibiting dark patterns and doomscrolling altogether would be too prohibitive. Many of the challenges consumers right now face could be resolved by enforcing existing regulation more effectively, she said.

She points to the fact that the EU has made a name for itself in the past by adding latest rules and regulations that have made it more difficult to access the European market, especially for small online businesses.

BEUC director Agustin Reyna disagrees.

"Instead of having 27 different regulations to adhere to, companies will now only get one," Reyna mentioned.

For him, this speaks for simplification, especially when the responsibility for compliance is shared between online influencers and the platforms they publish on.

According to the new legislation, the EU would have the possibility to impose fines of up to six percent of a tech giant's global annual revenue should the company violate the law.

The European Parliament and the Council, which represents member state governments, still have to agree on the text and formally adopt it. All experts agree that in that process, changes are still very likely.

Recent findings suggest that "It will be a difficult trialogue, especially in this climate of simplification and deregulation with a focus on strengthening European competitiveness," remarked Christoph Busch. In that climate, it is not easy to add consumer rights, he adds.

Industry observers note that agustin Reyna is more optimistic. "The parliament is a divided house, much more than in the past," he notes. "But consumer protection is a subject that brings parties together because it brings tangible outcomes to people.".

Daily briefing: Homo erectus had what it takes to thrive in the rainforest

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1219 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S.
  • Recent findings suggest that fossil teeth suggest that Homo erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago.
  • Artificial-intelligence giant Anthropic has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL.

Recent findings suggest that fossil teeth suggest that Homo erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago. Researchers had thought that these ancient hominins had been limited to savannahs and open woodlands, says Kira Westaway, a geochronologist and a co-author of two fresh studies. “This is a really big deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”.

Reference: Nature paper 1 & paper 2.

Artificial-intelligence giant Anthropic has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. The firm — now valued at a staggering US$1.5 trillion — has major ambitions in science. It made waves earlier this year when it reported that its model Claude had made several major mathematics breakthroughs. The company also introduced their first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research and has revealed plans to “substantially” scale up its work in AI-enabled drug discovery. Pitched as a company that prioritizes AI safety, some researchers question whether an IPO — and the accompanying investor demands — might disrupt some of Anthropic’s safety commitments.

Roughly 180 million people could be carrying a previously unknown type of giant virus in their guts. Researchers found DNA from these ‘egoviruses’ in gut samples from people, buffalo, goats, chickens, deer and pigs. Six clades were unique to people, one of which is estimated to be present in roughly 1% of the population. Microbiologists say that egoviruses could be the missing link between giant viruses that infect single-celled organisms and distantly related poxviruses, such as those that cause smallpox and mpox, which can infect people and animals directly.

Here in Washington DC, tens of thousands of researchers have gathered for the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting — a showcase for everything from neural implants to memory research.

Sources indicate that but when I asked a panel of leaders at the US National Institutes of Health what in neuroscience remains underappreciated, several pointed to the brain’s relationship with the rest of the body. Nora Volkow, director of the National Institute on Drug Abuse, lamented the lack of research into brain metabolism — a blind spot exposed by the surprising neurological effects of GLP-1 drugs.

Amy Bany Adams, acting director of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, offered a reminder of how much remains to be discovered. Of the glymphatic system, the brain’s waste-clearance network, she said: “We didn’t even know it existed when I was in graduate school.” I’m leaving with a longer list of questions about what else we’ve been overlooking.

Neuroscientists are uncovering how the brain orchestrates a tailored mixture of symptoms in response to either a bacterial or viral infection. Presenting at the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting on 15 November, researchers suggested that the brain decodes the type of pathogen that has invaded, accesses memories of past bouts of illness and can even mobilize immune defences at the sight of a sick person. The unpublished findings challenge the long-held view that neurological responses to infection are a one-size-fits-all response to inflammation.

Artificial-intelligence governance requires more than companies’ oversight of their models — it requires “a system of accountability” that works like a national constitution, argues legal scholar Cindy Skach. Firms should be held legally liable when individuals are affected by AI actions that infringe on their fundamental rights, Skach suggests. She proposes ‘human dignity’ as the most important value for the system to uphold. When a person’s dignity is violated — by an AI-generated deepfake or by a chatbot that treats a distressed user as just another interaction — they could petition a court directly to hold the perpetrator accountable.

Do you find networking a nightmare? Three experts share — in the form of short videos — how to grasp the nettle. They suggest thinking about networking as a professional skill that can be learnt and developed, considering arriving early for events and not worrying about volume. One high-quality connection and follow-up conversation is worth more than 100 business cards, says public-speaking coach Susie Ashfield.

In the second episode of Nature Podcast’s climate miniseries, host Nick Petrić Howe hears from scientists about what humanity can actually do to stop the runaway train of rising temperatures. The rise of renewable-energy technologies is already making a dent in greenhouse-gas emissions, experts say. But creating meat alternatives and a move away from an economic system that incentivizes ‘growth at any cost’ could help to really shift the dial.

Nature Podcast | 45 min listen or read the transcript.

In a recent development, vertebrate palaeontologist Aldo Benites-Palomino explains why the extinct ancient whale — which evolved extreme facial asymmetry to to make space in its head for echolocation and sound production organs — was named with a Peruvian word for “anything that is flashy, over-the-top, bizarre, extravagant or difficult to categorize aesthetically”. (Discover | 7 min read).

Reference: Communications Biology paper.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03797-3.

In a recent development, today I’m considering buying a prickly pear cactus (Opuntia) in case of a power cut. Researchers have found that the plants’ unusual method of photosynthesis can be harnessed to generate a small amount of electricity, with around eight prickly pears together generating nearly three times the voltage of a standard AA battery.

It has been revealed that your feedback on this newsletter gives me all the charge I need. Please send your thoughts to briefing@nature.com.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While there can be little doubt about Unai Emery’s status as an elite manager in the modern game, matches at the Nou Camp continue to be the stuff of nightmares.

His record at Barcelona now reads 15 defeats from 16 matches and this was another difficult evening with Aston Villa unable to banish the demons for the man who has transformed their club.

It was Emery’s 55th birthday and with the Prince of Wales and Prince George both in attendance, Villa fans were hopeful of another memorable European night. But from the moment midfielder João Gomes handed Barcelona their opening goal, it was always going to be an uphill struggle.

Emery has suffered many uncomfortable occasions at this grand old stadium, none more so than the notorious “La Remontada” of 2017 when he last competed here in the Champions League with Paris St-Germain.

Recent findings suggest that this latest visit would become his heaviest defeat in Europe as Villa manager. With three wins from the opening four matches, they still have a fine chance of progressing to the knockout stage. Yet, aside from the mistakes, there will be a sense that Villa could have capitalised more against a team in the midst of a defensive injury crisis. They did have a number of chances in the first half but were left to rue their lack of ruthlessness.

At the heart of Barcelona’s victory was Lamine Yamal, their outstanding jewel from the academy. The 19-year-old became the highest-scoring teenager in Champions League history, eclipsing the record of 13 he previously shared with Kylian Mbappé, with the opening goal.

Yamal was orchestrating everything from the pace of the match to the volume of the supporters, at one point imploring them to raise the noise in the first half with both arms aloft.

There was also another impressive performance from England international Anthony Gordon and Raphinha, who dedicated his two goals to the memory of Jesus de Miguel, the Tenerife forward, who died on Tuesday.

With that tragedy fresh in the minds and the Nou Camp under construction, it was a peculiar atmosphere at times.

The defeat marked the end of Villa’s 100 per cent record in the competition, with a tough test away at Galatasaray up next before they host PSG in December. They remain high up in the table and have often displayed a propensity to bounce back promptly from defeats.

Industry observers note that emery stated: “We are in a process and this was a very good test against a team like Barcelona. We are not at the level we want to achieve but there are a lot of experiences for us to take. Overall, we are competing fantastically in the Champions League and there is still work to do.

Recent findings suggest that “Over the process we’ve had here, we have made mistakes but then overcame them. We accept this defeat but take a lot of information from it.”.

Nine years have passed since Emery’s last visit in this competition and time has not proved a great healer.

Industry observers note that then in charge of PSG, Emery witnessed his team surrender a 4-0 first-leg lead to lose 6-5 on aggregate. Any matches where he is involved at the Nou Camp will revive memories of that remarkable comeback. He must have feared a repeat of more pain when Yamal, making his 37th Champions League appearance, rewarded Barcelona’s early pressure.

It has been revealed that villa’s defending needed to be as close to perfect as possible, but they were exposed after a poor error of judgment from Gomes. Under pressure from Barcelona’s attackers, Gomes panicked and played a blind pass into the path of Yamal, who bent his left-footed shot into the corner.

Recent findings suggest that that mistake could have threatened to damage confidence but Villa did respond. Matty Cash’s half-volley from inside the penalty area was only a few inches wide, while Johan Manzambi side-footed wide of the goal after a quick break down the right from Nicolas Jackson.

Recent findings suggest that with Andreas Christensen, Eric García, Xavi Espart and Jules Koundé all absent here, Barcelona’s defence did appear vulnerable. Jackson was targeting the flanks and having his more dangerous moments challenging their high line. Emery paced his technical area, imploring his players to remain focused.

Yet Barcelona’s forward three were always a threat and they increased their lead eight minutes into the second half. Raphinha was given too much room to turn in the penalty area and his shot took a heavy deflection off the heel of Pau Torres to find the bottom corner. Emery was furious, appearing to raise his fist in the air at another poor goal conceded.

Raphinha doubles Barcelona's lead with his 18th goal of the season! 🔥 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/NzFPYVzDuj.

Barcelona added a third goal with Raphinha converting from close range after a sublime pass from João Cancelo.

Raphinha dedicated his goals to De Miguel, who died on Tuesday after sustaining serious injuries during a match the previous night. He said: “Tonight I don’t want to talk about football. I want to send a lot of strength to Jesus de Miguel’s family.

“May he rest in peace. In the end, this can happen to anyone. The truth is that it’s very tough. When we saw the news this morning, it was complicated. I’m incredibly shocked and sad. In the end, you go to play a match, and the same thing could happen to you. From myself, from the club, we want to send a lot of strength to his family.”.

Villa did continue to fight for a consolation, with substitute Leon Goretzka heading against the post and their 3,000 travelling fans continued to sing in the rain after the final whistle.

This was the first encounter between the two clubs since the European Super Cup Final in January 1983, and yet another reminder of the upward trajectory under Emery.

Aston Villa have made the trip over to Spain to take on Barcelona in the Champions League on matchday four. These teams last met all the way back in 1983, when they met in the European Super Cup. Barcelona won the first leg 1-0 at home before Aston Villa claimed a 3-0 victory at Villa Park, meaning Villa progressed 3-1 on aggregate.

Recent findings suggest that aston Villa have made the perfect start to their Champions League campaign, winning all three games, beating Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking, scoring 12 goals in the process. Unai Emery’s side drew 1-1 at home against Fulham in the league on Saturday. Emery, who celebrates his 55th birthday today, has a very dismal record against Barcelona, taking just three wins from 30 matches. His last Champions League game at the Nou Camp was infamous as his PSG side lost 6-1 to go out in the last 16 back in 2017 despite winning the first leg of that tie 4-0.

According to recent reports, “In 1982, Villa won the European Cup, and we like to think about playing in this competition again and trying to repeat that success,” Emery stated. “Barcelona are favourites for what they have done in the last ten years; now they need to prove why they are favourites.

Recent findings suggest that “[Barcelona] have [Lamine] Yamal. He is a special player. You can see in him as a player who could end up being the best. He needs a few things but he could end up being a great player. Rodri gives personality to the team. They have [Anthony] Gordon giving them speed and hard work. They have Pedri or Fermin [Lopez] as offensive midfielders.”.

It has been revealed that barcelona started strongly in the Champions League, winning their first two games, but lost 4-2 at defending champions PSG last time out. They warmed up for this match with an emphatic 6-1 win over Alaves in La Liga on Saturday. That victory gives them a two-point lead at the summit of La Liga.

Industry observers note that “We know that at this level, anything can happen,” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick said. “Against Real Madrid, the result could have been different. These are special matches, but we are staying confident. It is normal to focus more on our last two defeats, but I have confidence in my team, which indicated it again on Saturday. Now, we are focused on the Champions League, with the goal of finishing in the top eight. For me, he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world and he has reaped extraordinary successes. His team’s style of play is clear and very well organised. Just look at how they execute set pieces; it is something impressive. Their confidence in themselves is unmatched. It will be a tough match against a great team and a great coach.”.

#25555. 'He's creating a culture I've never seen before': Aston Villa star AMADOU ONANA reveals how Unai Emery influenced his upcoming contract, his 'lonely, dark' road back from injury - and why he's learning a sixth language

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1600 w)
📖 Baca
